The 10-minute build: Banana
If Halloween is closer than you think, here is the whole build, word for word from the costume guide.
The pick: Banana
Real numbers: 10 min - Easy
You will need:
Yellow sweatshirt and sweatpants, 1 set (make: from closet, or buy: clothing store)
Green felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
Headband, 1 (buy: dollar store)
Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
Put on the yellow sweatshirt and sweatpants.
Cut a stem shape from green felt, about 4 inches tall.
Hold the stem against the headband and check the position in a mirror BEFORE gluing, once fabric glue sets, the stem cannot be moved. Glue the stem to the headband and let it dry flat.
Wear the headband. You are a banana.
Optional pro finish: glue a small brown felt rectangle at the bottom front of the sweatshirt as the banana tip. Top and bottom details make it read as banana, not yellow sweats.
Build this costume →

FAQ
What is an easy DIY Halloween costume for kids?
The Banana takes 10 minutes: a yellow sweatsuit and sweatpants plus a green felt stem hat on a headband. Underneath it is just pajamas, so it is the easiest costume a kid will actually keep on. The full step-by-step build is on this page.
What are good last-minute Halloween costume ideas?
The Classic Ghost takes 10 minutes: a white sheet, a thick black marker, and scissors. Cut the eye holes small first and trim the hem so it clears the ground. If you can make one store trip, the Glow Skeleton takes 20 minutes, and it glows so drivers can see your kid on dark streets.
What are good group Halloween costume ideas?
The Cereal Crew is the simplest group build: each kid becomes a different cereal box in 20 minutes. For the whole family, the Aussie Dog Family is blue and orange shirts plus paper ears on headbands, 25 minutes. Two sisters can do Snow Sisters: one icy blue dress, one pink, 30 minutes.
How much does it cost to make a kids Halloween costume?
Every pick on this page builds from household basics. If the shopping list is the whole question, the Cereal Crew needs one cereal box per kid and the Classic Ghost needs only a white sheet.
Can I make a Halloween costume the night before?
Yes, if you pick a build . The Banana and the Classic Ghost both take 10 minutes and nothing has to dry, so they work at 8pm on October 30. The Fuzzy Monster and Snow Sisters need glue or paint to dry, so start those a few hours earlier.

If Halloween is closer than you think, here is the whole build, word for word from the costume guide.
The pick: Cereal Crew
Real numbers: 20 min - Easy
You will need:
Solid-color shirt and pants per person, 1 set each (own)
Empty cereal boxes, 1 per person (make: save from home)
Markers or crayons in assorted colors, 1 pack (own)
String, about 4 feet per person (own)
Scissors, 1 pair
Tape, 1 roll
Each person invents a cereal name.
Open the box along the side seam.
Flatten it before cutting.
Cut the front panel off an empty cereal box.
Keep it large.
Decorate the panel with the markers.
Draw a mascot, add a prize burst, and write the name big.
Tape string to the top corners of each panel.
Wear the panel over a plain shirt like a sandwich board.
Optional pro finish: add a prize-inside burst and a fake nutrition joke in the corner.

The pick: Deadpan Diva

Mom goes as the beekeeper in white with a mesh veil; the kid wears yellow and black stripes with antennae. Twenty-five minutes, no sewing.
The veil sells the beekeeper, the stripes sell the bee, and together they read in a single glance. The mom side is a white shirt from the closet.
Real numbers: 25 min - Easy

If: The kid wants to be the hero
The pick: Little Lifeguard
Kid gets the red tee, whistle, and pool-noodle rescue buoy; mom goes as the beachgoer in a sundress and sunglasses, pure closet. Twenty minutes, no sewing.
The whistle is real, the buoy is a pool noodle, and the whole thing reads official at a glance. Mom's costume is literally getting dressed.

The full build: Beekeeper & Bee
If Halloween is closer than you think, here is the whole build, word for word from the costume guide.
The pick: Beekeeper & Bee
Real numbers: 25 min - Easy
You will need:
White long-sleeve shirt and white pants, 1 set (own, or buy: thrift store)
Fine mesh fabric or a mosquito head net, 1 (buy: craft store or camping aisle)
Wide-brim hat, 1 (own, or buy: dollar store)
Yellow shirt and yellow pants, 1 set (own, or buy: thrift store)
Black electrical tape, 1 roll (buy: dollar store)
Black pipe cleaners for antennae, 2 (buy: craft store)
Headband, 1 (buy: dollar store, or use your own)
Yellow and black face paint sticks, 1 set (buy: craft store)
Scissors, 1 pair
Beekeeper: drape the mesh over the hat.
Tie it at the neck.
Cut the face opening wide first.
Trim it after a fitting.
Bee: wrap 3 to 4 black tape stripes around the yellow shirt and pants.
Press the tape flat so the edges stay down.
Bend the pipe cleaners into a V.
Tape them to the headband for antennae.
Add two black face-paint dots on the cheeks.
Safety: Cut the veil opening wide enough that vision stays clear, and tie nothing tight around the neck. Use tape, not string, for the stripes so nothing unravels.
The adult is the beekeeper, since the mesh limits vision.
The smaller of the two is the bee.
Optional pro finish: the beekeeper carries a small cardboard sign that says HONEY.
Build this costume →
Read the full step-by-step guide

FAQ
Do I really not have to build my own costume?
For the lifeguard pair, no: the beachgoer is a sundress and sunglasses. For the others, the mom side is one closet outfit plus one small piece: a shaker top, a veil, or a bottle cap.
What if my kid will not wear their half?
Pick the pair where the kid half builds on their normal clothes: the bee stripes go on a yellow shirt they already wear, and the lifeguard is a red tee. Nothing new touching the skin is the rule.
What does each build guide show?
Salt and Pepper, Ketchup and Mustard, Beekeeper and Bee, Little Lifeguard: every guide lists the build time and the full materials list, closet items first.
Can we build these the night before?
Yes. The longest is Beekeeper and Bee at 25 minutes. the shaker tops need time to dry, so build those first.

What Should My Baby Be for Halloween? 5 Easy DIY Baby Costumes
Quick answer: Fuzzy Monster (15 min, 1 pastel fuzzy sweatsuit), Pocket Plush Monster (25 min, fuzzy one-piece pajamas or sweatsuit), and Bumble Bee (20 min, black sweatshirt and sweatpants): all built around the baby's comfort. Tap any name for its full build guide: materials list, numbered steps, and safety notes.
Updated September 2026
Every build is comfort-first: no face coverings, no itchy seams, no sewing. All under 30 minutes.

Three more nap-time formulas
Not full guides: the whole formula for each, hot glue only, no sewing. Built on onesies you already own.
Formula: Sleepy owl
Brown footed sleeper. Hot-glue rows of felt feather scallops down the front, then glue two big sleepy eyes to the hood. Nothing on the face at all; the hood does the work.
Formula: Cotton-ball sheep
White onesie. Hot-glue cotton balls all over the torso, then glue two black felt ears to a soft headband. Skip the headband if they pull it off; the cotton-ball onesie reads sheep on its own.
Formula: Strawberry
Red onesie. Hot-glue a green felt leaf collar around the neck and dot yellow felt seeds across the front. The collar is the whole costume; the seeds take five minutes.
The full build: Baby Dinosaur
If Halloween is closer than you think, here is the whole build, word for word from the costume guide.
The pick: Baby Dinosaur
Real numbers: 20 min - Easy
You will need:
Green hoodie, 1 (buy: clothing store, or use your own)
2 sheets green craft felt, 9x12 inches each (buy: craft store, construction paper works too)
Pillow stuffing or 2 old socks (make: stuff from home)
Safety pins, 6 to 8 (buy: dollar store)
Masking tape, 1 roll
Scissors, 1 pair
Cut a paper triangle first.
Test the size on the hoodie.
Cut 6 to 8 big triangles from the green felt.
Tape the spikes in a row down the back of the hoodie.
Pin each spike from inside the hoodie.
Stuff the old socks with the pillow stuffing.
Tape the open ends of the socks shut.
Safety: Pin everything from inside the green hoodie, so pin backs face the fabric and never the skin.
Pin the stuffed tail to the back waistband of the hoodie.
Optional pro finish: cut two small white felt triangles and pin them to the cuffs as claws.
Build this costume →
Read the full step-by-step guide

FAQ
Are these really no-sew?
Yes. Every guide on this page was checked against its materials list and build steps: no sewing verbs, no needles, no machines. The builds use cutting, gluing, taping, pinning, and tying only. The three bonus formulas at the bottom are hot glue only.
What should the costume go over?
A onesie or footed sleeper they already own and like. Build on the base layer, not the baby: nothing new should touch their skin except what already does.
Is face paint safe for babies?
Skip it for babies. Every pick on this page reads clearly without paint. The Glow Skeleton guide adds a face paint step for older kids. Skip that step for babies.
How long will a nap-time build actually take?
The five guides run 15 to 20 minutes of hands-on time; the fuzzy monster needs time to dry after. Cut the felt during one nap, glue during the next.

Common questions
How do group costume packs work?
Each pack is one theme your whole crew builds from what is at home. Open any idea for its free build guide with the timed build time and materials up front - no matching outfits to buy.
What is a good couples costume?
Pick a pair with built-in contrast so the two halves read together. The couples section above has the full list, and every idea links to its own build guide.
What about a whole classroom or trunk-or-treat team?
The classroom and trunk-or-treat sections have big-group themes where one base idea scales to the whole group, with room for everyone to be a little different.
What does each build guide show?
Every guide lists its materials and its timed build time up front, so the whole crew knows the plan before anyone starts.

Halloween costume contest is ON: Friday Oct 30, winners announced at the all-hands.
Categories: Funniest, Most Creative, Best DIY, Best Duo.
Need a costume? Take the 2-minute quiz. It picks one you can build from stuff at home: https://pickmycostume.com/?src=collection-office

Copy text
FAQ
What are good categories for an office costume contest?
Pick four or five: Funniest, Most Creative, Best DIY, Best Duo or Team, Most Desk-Friendly, and a light Scariest. Fewer categories mean every vote counts.
How do you vote in an office costume contest fairly?
One ballot per person, no voting for yourself, anonymous tally. For small teams, a three-person judging panel beats a popular vote.
Do you need prizes for an office costume contest?
No, but they help turnout. Leave early on a Friday, a coffee card, and a traveling trophy cover it. Keep the budget under $25.
What if nobody at the office wants to dress up?
Keep it opt-in and give people an easy on-ramp. A 2-minute costume quiz that builds a costume from things at home removes the biggest excuse, which is not having an idea.
How do you include remote workers in a costume contest?
Photo parade in a shared thread, a 24-hour voting window for every timezone, winners announced on a video call, and the prize shipped by email.
Should an office costume contest be mandatory?
No. Voluntary contests with good categories get higher turnout than forced ones, and mandatory dress-up punishes tight budgets and real objections.
How many contest categories is too many?
Six is the ceiling and four or five is the sweet spot. Every category needs at least three real contenders or the win feels hollow.
What is the best way to announce contest winners?
At the all-hands or in the main team channel, one line per winner saying what they won and why. Copy the Slack announcement above and paste it as-is.
Still deciding? Take the 2-minute quiz and get one picked for you.

Common questions
How many costume guides are there?
169, A to Z. Every one is a free step-by-step DIY build guide.
What does each guide include?
The real build time, materials, and effort level up front, then the full materials list and steps. The numbers come straight from each guide.
Can I make one of these tonight?
Yes. 17 of the 169 need nothing new, or just 1 or 2 extra supplies, if you have the basic supplies at home. The closet page lists all 17. Fast builds are a bigger group: 126 of the 169 take 30 minutes or less of work.
How do I pick one?
Take the 2-minute quiz and get one personal pick, or browse A-Z and open anything that catches your eye.

Classic Ghost vs Classic Vampire: head to head
Two easy DIY costumes, head to head. Classic Ghost is the fastest (10 min). Classic Ghost can be made tonight with stuff you already own. Only the Classic Ghost works for young kids. Every one is rated Easy in our build guides and links to a full step-by-step below. Numbers come straight from our costume bank, which is what powers the Pick My Costume quiz.

The trade-offs, in plain English
Classic Ghost: 10 min, nothing to buy beyond the assumed basics. Top five for kids and adults alike. The most universal costume there is.
Classic Vampire: 25 min, needs 4 store items. Scary with 25 minutes of effort and it photographs great.

Common questions
Where do these rankings come from?
The top 10 comes from Google's Frightgeist, which ranks costumes from Google Search data - the ranking shown is Frightgeist's latest published one, from October 2026. The 2026 list ranks the top trending costumes, the biggest search spikes of the year. The 'Trending on Pick My Costume' grid is the 8 costumes our own visitors saved and picked most in recent weeks.
How often is this page updated?
The on-site grid refreshes weekly from our own saves and picks. The national top 10 updates when Google publishes new Frightgeist rankings.
Can I make these costumes at home?
Every costume in the on-site grid has a free step-by-step DIY build guide - tap any card to open it. Each guide lists the real build time, materials, and effort level.
How do I see what a costume looks like on me?
Take the 2-minute quiz to get a personal pick, then tap Try it on on the result card and upload a front-facing photo. The preview runs on your device and the photo never leaves your phone.

## Page: https://pickmycostume.com/privacy

🎃 Pick My Costume
Take the quiz
Privacy
Effective: November 9, 2026
Pick My Costume is a free Halloween costume picker with no account, no login, and no email required. This policy explains what we collect and what we don't.
What we collect
Anonymous usage counts. We count events like quiz completions and button taps so we can see which parts of the site work. They carry a random ID, not your name, email, or account. Nothing that identifies you.
Your email, only if you ask. Tapping “Email me this plan” sends your address to our server for the sole purpose of sending that one email with your costume plan.
Oct 27 reminder (only if you tick the box). If you also tick “Remind me Oct 27,” we keep your address until October 27, 2027, to send you one reminder email that morning with last-minute ideas you can make that night. That is it: one plan email, plus one reminder only if you asked for it. We delete reminder addresses right after October 27. We never sell your address, never add it to any other list, and never use it for anything you did not ask for. Want it deleted sooner? Email [email protected] and a human will remove it.
Typed costume names (structural only). If you type a custom costume name, the text itself never leaves your device; we only record that the feature was used.
Costume searches (anonymous). When you search for a costume, we log the first 30 characters of your search term with a random ID, never your name, so we can see which costumes people look for and add the ones we are missing.
What we don't collect
Your individual quiz answers stay in your browser. We record which costume ideas get shown and picked, in aggregate, without tying them to you.
We don't ask for, and don't store, names, phone numbers, or locations.
No ads. Analytics goes only to PostHog, our own analytics provider, to count usage. Never sold or shared with advertisers.
How long we keep things
Anonymous usage counts are kept as long as they are useful for improving the site. Email addresses for the Oct 27 reminder are deleted right after October 27, 2027. If you ask us to delete your address sooner, we will.
AI assistants and connectors
If you use Pick My Costume through an AI assistant (like ChatGPT or Claude), the connector only reads our public costume guides, the same pages anyone can open. It does not log your questions or store anything about you.
Cookies
The site may store small values in your browser's local storage so the quiz remembers where you left off. Nothing in local storage is sent anywhere.
Children
The site is for parents and adults. We don't knowingly collect information from children under 13; email features (the plan email and the optional Oct 27 reminder) are for adults.
Contact
Questions about this policy or the site: [email protected] .

You need no account or login.
The quiz asks five short questions.
It returns three costume picks.
Each pick links to a build guide.
Your answers choose your three picks.
Picks come from 169 costume ideas.
Guides and photos
Guides list time, effort, and steps.
Guides split supplies three ways.
Buy, tools, and already at home.
Photos are AI-generated concept images.
They show the look, not a guarantee.
Follow every safety step in each guide.
Use your own judgment for your family.
Adults should help kids with sharp tools.
Buying your supplies
We take no payment from you.
We place no orders for you.
Guide lists name things to buy.
You choose where to buy them.
Stores set prices, and prices change.
Accounts and data
You need no email to use it.
Email is only for plans you request.
See the Privacy page for full details.
AI tools read only public guides.
They do not log your questions.
No guarantees
This site is provided as is.

Times and effort are honest estimates.
Your build may take longer.
We are not liable for any loss.

## Page: https://pickmycostume.com/office-contest-guide

How to run an office Halloween costume contest
Quick answer: Soccer Squad (25 min, matching jerseys or same-color t-shirts), Web Hero Crew (30 min, hoodies in red), and Emoji Crew (15 min, 1 yellow t-shirt per person): built to win the office vote. Tap any name for its full build guide: materials list, numbered steps, and safety notes.
Updated September 29, 2026 for Halloween 2026. New this season: the quiz bank behind every ballot link is up to 169 costume ideas, and this guide was rechecked against this year's contest dates.
So the contest landed on your desk. Good news: a great office costume contest takes about 20 minutes of setup and one honest rule sheet. This is the whole playbook - timeline, categories, fair voting, prizes that cost nothing, and the three messages you need to send. Plus a free contest tool that prints your ballots and tallies your votes.
Timeline Categories Fair rules Voting Prizes Announcements Remote workers FAQ
1. The timeline
Work backwards from contest day, which is usually Friday, October 30. Three checkpoints are all you need.
Three weeks out: announce the contest, the date, and the categories. Give people the costume quiz link ( office-friendly costume ideas help too) so nobody can say they had no idea what to wear.
One week out: send the reminder with the voting plan - where ballots go, when the parade happens, when winners are announced. Half your turnout comes from this message.
Contest day: run the parade in the morning, collect ballots by mid-afternoon, announce winners at the all-hands or in the main channel. Done.
2. Pick four or five categories
Categories are the contest. Pick ones people can win without spending money, and every entry feels like it has a shot.
Funniest
The easiest category to enter and the most fun to judge. The Error 404 costume - a white t-shirt, markers, tape - wins this regularly because it is a joke the whole office gets.
Most Creative
For the builder. The person who turned a cardboard box into something unrecognizable takes this home.
Best DIY
The budget category: built at home from closet basics, and the materials list is part of the judging. This is where the closet-built costumes shine.
Best Duo or Team
Pairs and groups: Bacon and Eggs, Salt and Pepper, the Block Party Duo. Team entries pull in the people who would never dress up alone.
Most Desk-Friendly
The work-appropriate category: readable on a video call, comfortable in a chair, no fake blood, nothing that beeps during standup. Coffee Cup territory.
Scariest, lightly
Keep it light for the office: spooky, not gory. A glow skeleton beats anything with fake blood, which is banned at most desks anyway.
Rule of thumb: every category needs at least three real contenders or the win feels hollow. If turnout looks small, shrink to three categories.
3. Rules that keep it fair
Post the rules with the announcement. Five lines is enough, and it heads off every argument.
One ballot per person. No ballot-stuffing for your desk neighbor.
No voting for yourself. The most argued rule, so state it up front.
Work-appropriate only. If it would not survive an HR glance, it does not enter.
Teams enter team categories. A duo does not also sweep the solo categories.
Tally is anonymous. You announce the winners, not the vote counts. Close counts stay private.
One more call for small teams: under about 15 people, use a three-person judging panel instead of a popular vote. Popular votes in small offices turn into popularity contests. A panel of two managers and one neutral party is harder to argue with.
4. Voting that fits your office
Match the method to the room. All three work.
The ballot box
Print ballots, drop a box by the kitchen, collect by 3pm. Lowest tech, highest participation, because it takes ten seconds. The free contest tool prints ballots with your categories filled in.
The Slack or Teams vote
Post each contender as a photo with a number, then a 24-hour emoji window: react to vote. Great for hybrid teams because remote people vote on equal footing.
The show of hands
Parade at the all-hands, cheer-meter for each entry. Loud, fast, and slightly unfair to quiet costumes - use it for the fun categories, not the judged ones.
5. Prizes people actually want
The prize budget for an office contest stays small, and honestly the trophy is the thing. What wins:
Leave early on a Friday. Costs nothing, valued above everything.
A coffee card. Universally correct.
The traveling trophy. A plastic crown or a printed certificate that lives on the winner's desk until next Halloween. The contest tool prints winner sheets; the certificate is the part people photograph.
Lunch with the boss. Cheap for the company, weirdly coveted.
Skip: big-ticket prizes (they make the runners-up resentful), gag prizes that punch down, and prizes for "best" anything that reward spending money.
6. The three messages, already written
Copy, paste, done. Fill in the bracketed bits.
The kickoff
Halloween costume contest is ON: [Friday, October 30]. Winners announced at the all-hands.
Categories: Funniest, Most Creative, Best DIY, Best Duo or Team, Most Desk-Friendly.
Rules: one ballot per person, no voting for yourself, work-appropriate only.
Need a costume idea? Take the 2-minute quiz - it picks one you can build from stuff at home: https://pickmycostume.com/
Ballots, rules, and the whole setup: https://pickmycostume.com/office-contest-kit
Copy text
Copied. Paste it wherever your office plans things.
The one-week reminder
One week until the costume contest, [Friday]! Ballots go in the box by the kitchen by 3pm, parade at the morning standup.
Still need a costume? The quiz takes 2 minutes and everything starts from the closet: https://pickmycostume.com/
Work-friendly ideas if you want a head start: https://pickmycostume.com/office-costumes

Costume contest results are in! Thanks to everyone who entered.
Funniest: [name] as [costume]

Best Duo or Team: [names] as [costume]
Most Desk-Friendly: [name] as [costume]
The traveling trophy lives on [winner]'s desk until next Halloween. See you all next year.
Copy text
Copied.
7. Including remote workers
Remote people get skipped by office contests more than anything else. The fix is a photo parade, and it takes ten minutes.
Photo thread: remote workers post a costume photo in a shared thread by the same 3pm deadline.
24-hour voting window: emoji or form voting stays open a full day so every timezone gets a turn.
Announce on video: read the winners on a call, not just in chat, so remote people are in the room for it.
Ship the prize: a coffee card by email takes two minutes. Remote winners who get nothing tell the story for a year.
8. The people who skip dressing up
Every office has them, and the contest is better when they are not pressured. Two things actually move the needle:
Never make it mandatory. Mandatory fun is not fun, and it punishes tight budgets and real objections. Voluntary contests get higher turnout than forced ones.
Give them the easy on-ramp. The biggest excuse is not having an idea. A 2-minute quiz that builds a costume from what is already at home kills that excuse in one link.
Running the contest, not just reading about it? The free office contest kit turns this page into a tool: enter contestant names, print ballots, tap-tally the votes, and print the winner sheet. No account, prints clean.
FAQ
What are good categories for an office costume contest?
Pick four or five: Funniest, Most Creative, Best DIY, Best Duo or Team, Most Desk-Friendly, and a light Scariest. Fewer categories mean every vote counts.
How do you vote in an office costume contest fairly?
One ballot per person, no voting for yourself, anonymous tally. For small teams, a three-person judging panel beats a popular vote.
Do you need prizes for an office costume contest?
No, but they help turnout. Leave early on a Friday, a coffee card, and a traveling trophy cover it. Keep the budget small.
What if nobody at the office wants to dress up?
Keep it opt-in and give people an easy on-ramp. A 2-minute costume quiz that builds a costume from things at home removes the biggest excuse, which is not having an idea.
How do you include remote workers in a costume contest?
Photo parade in a shared thread, a 24-hour voting window for every timezone, winners announced on a video call, and the prize shipped by email.
Should an office costume contest be mandatory?
No. Voluntary contests with good categories get higher turnout than forced ones, and mandatory dress-up punishes tight budgets and real objections.
How many contest categories is too many?
Six is the ceiling and four or five is the sweet spot. Every category needs at least three real contenders or the win feels hollow.
What is the best way to announce contest winners?
At the all-hands or in the main team channel, one line per winner saying what they won and why. Use the winners template above and paste it as-is.
Handing this to your team? Send them the 2-minute quiz first, the contest runs itself after that.

## Page: https://pickmycostume.com/hand-me-down

Pick My Costume
Last year's costume is this year's parts list
Which costume do you already own?
Browse all 169 ideas
Change
Quick answer: Emoji Crew (15 min, 1 yellow t-shirt per person), Classic Ghost (10 min, 1 white flat sheet), and Fairy Tale Princesses (15 min, 1 dress from the closet per person): ranked by how many parts you already own. Tap any name for its full build guide: materials list, numbered steps, and safety notes.
Pick the costume already sitting in your closet. We rank all 169 ideas by the parts you already own, so this year builds faster.
Show all matches
Copy my hand-me-down plan
We count exact parts, not vibes. Green paper is not red paper. Parts that match by material but not color are shown separately as "same kind", so there are no surprises. We skip the craft-drawer basics (scissors, tape, cardboard, foil, socks, paper and pen). Everybody has those, so they do not change the ranking.
How this works
Does this work if last year's costume was store-bought?
If it was mostly store-bought, there are no homemade parts to match, and the page will tell you so honestly. It works best with DIY builds: capes, wings, face paint, cardboard props, and costumes made from old clothes.
What counts as a matching part?
Exact matches are the same material, like green felt to green felt. Same-kind matches are the same material in a different color, like green paper to red paper. Those are shown separately because you will still need the new color. Craft-drawer basics like scissors and tape are never counted.
Can I pass a costume down to a younger sibling instead?
Yes. The parts do not care who wears them. Pick the older kid's costume above and the ranking works the same. Check the build guide for sizing notes before you start.
Free, no signup. Built with Muse.

Costumes From Your Closet

Updated September 2026
The cheapest costume is the one you never have to shop for. Tick off what you already own and we will show you which of our 169 costume ideas are ready to build from your closet.
Out of 169 costume ideas, 17 need zero to two supplies beyond the default household basics : scissors, tape, markers, paper and pen, aluminum foil, cardboard, a white t-shirt, a plain t-shirt, black clothes, an old bedsheet, a pillowcase, and socks. Tick everything in your house. Your matches update as you go.

3. Closet-costume questions
What Halloween costume can I make from clothes I already own? Tick off what you own in the matcher above and it ranks all 169 costume ideas by what you can build. Out of 169 ideas, 17 need zero to two supplies beyond default household basics (scissors, tape, markers, cardboard, old clothes, paper). The Classic Ghost needs only an old bedsheet, a marker, and scissors.
How many costumes can I make without shopping at all? Two with just the 12 assumed household basics: the Classic Ghost and the Emoji Crew. Fifteen more need just one or two extra supplies, like red paper or glue.
What is the easiest closet costume for a kid? The Classic Ghost: 10 minutes, easy. An old bedsheet, a thick black marker, and scissors. Cut the eye holes small first, you can always widen them.
What about the KPop Demon Hunters trend? The Neon Demon Hunter is the top-ranked idea in the bank for 2026. Start with a black hoodie and pants from the closet, add neon face paint, and grab a foam sword and glow-in-the-dark tattoos for the full look.
Do I need to buy anything to use this page? No. It is free with no signup. Every costume shows exactly what you still need, or nothing at all, and each card links to its full step-by-step build guide.
Still deciding?
Take the 2-minute quiz and get one pick matched to your vibe, budget, and timeline.

Dinosaur Land
Dinosaur Costume Ideas
Quick answer: start with the Baby Dinosaur (20 min; green hoodie, felt spikes, stuffed tail), the Dino Tourist (10 min; Hawaiian shirt, dino tail, fanny pack), or the Raptor Barista (10 min; dino snout hood, tiny T. rex arms). Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
All 10 Dinosaur Land costumes
Dinosaur Land is the roaring heart of the Costume Galaxy, home to ten dinosaur costumes that run from sweet to silly. Classic species builds like the Baby Dino and the Raptor share the region with joke costumes like the Dino Tourist and the Raptor Barista, plus group builds that turn the whole family into a dino pack. Most costumes center on a hoodie, felt spikes, and a stuffed tail, which makes this the friendliest region for first-time DIY builders. It suits toddlers who only want to roar, dino-obsessed kids, and parents who need something cute in under half an hour.

The Food Court
Food Costume Ideas
Quick answer: start with the Pizza Slice (45 min; cardboard triangle, felt pepperoni), the Banana (10 min; yellow sweatsuit, green felt stem hat), or the Ketchup & Mustard (15 min; red and yellow bottle tunics). Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
All 31 Food Court costumes
The Food Court is the tastiest corner of the Costume Galaxy, with thirty-one food costumes that turn dinner into a punchline. Pizza slices, tacos, sushi, donuts, and bananas all live here, alongside couple costumes like Ketchup and Mustard and group builds such as a picnic spread or a cereal box crew. Most are built from cardboard, felt, and thrift-store basics, so a convincing costume can come together the night before. It suits funny families, couples who want a matching joke, and anyone who would rather wear the snack than eat it. Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.

Princess Castle
Princess & Fairy Tale Costume Ideas
Quick answer: start with the Fairy Tale Princesses (15 min; a dress or crown from the closet), the Prince & Princess (10 min; crown and cape, thrifted gown and tiara), or the Garden Fairy (20 min; tulle wings, flower crown, wand). Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
All 13 Princess Castle costumes
Princess Castle is the royal wing of the Costume Galaxy, with thirteen fairy tale and princess costumes fit for a throne room. Royal gowns, tiaras, fairy wings, witches, and mermaids live here, from the classic Fairy Tale Princess to group builds like Prince and Princess or a fairy sisterhood. Most builds start with a dress from the closet plus a crown, cape, or tulle wings, which keeps the crafting simple and the twirl factor high. It suits kids who have a favorite storybook hero, siblings who want matching magic, and anyone chasing happily-ever-after. Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.

🎃 Pick My Costume
Pick my costume
Fright Night
Scary DIY Halloween Costumes
Quick answer: start with the Classic Ghost (10 min; white sheet, cut-out eyes), the Classic Vampire (25 min; black cape, fangs), or the Zombie Coworker (20 min; torn button-down, pale makeup). Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
All 19 Fright Night costumes
Fright Night is the spooky district of the Costume Galaxy, where nineteen scary costumes lurk. Classic ghosts, vampires, zombies, witches, and haunted-house creatures live here, from the sheet-simple Classic Ghost to joke-scary builds like the Zombie Coworker. Most are black clothing, pale makeup, and felt or cardboard details, so the fright is more fun than effort. It suits kids who want to be properly scary, teens planning a haunted hallway, and adults who take Halloween seriously. Sensitive dressers and tiny kids may prefer Silly Street instead. Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.

Pick my costume
Hero Headquarters
Superhero Costume Ideas
Quick answer: start with the Superhero Family (30 min; red sweatsuits, black eye masks, felt logo), the Backyard Superhero (15 min; short cape, first initial on the chest), or the Cardboard Knight (60 min; silver-painted cardboard armor, pool-noodle sword). Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
All 14 Hero Headquarters costumes
Hero Headquarters is where the Costume Galaxy keeps its capes: fourteen superhero costumes for solo saviors and whole teams. Family superhero squads, backyard heroes, knights, and masked crusaders live here, built from sweatsuits, capes, felt masks, and cardboard armor. It is the strongest region for group coordination, because matching colors and a shared emblem make the photo. It suits siblings who want to team up, kids who never take the cape off, and parents joining the mission. Most builds take thirty minutes or less. Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
Superhero Family 30 min · Easy

Pick my costume
Animal Kingdom
Animal Costume Ideas
Quick answer: start with the Bumble Bee (20 min; black sweats, yellow tape stripes, felt antennae), the Little Lion (20 min; tan sweatsuit, fuzzy mane hood), or the Cat & Mouse (15 min; cat ears versus mouse ears). Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
All 16 Animal Kingdom costumes
Animal Kingdom is the wild side of the Costume Galaxy, home to sixteen animal costumes from barnyard to jungle. Bumble bees, lions, cats, sharks, pups, and jungle creatures live here, most built from sweatsuits in the right color plus felt ears, tails, and stripes. It is one of the easiest regions for toddlers, because a cozy onesie-style build doubles as warm pajamas. It suits animal-obsessed kids, sibling pairs like Cat and Mouse, and anyone who wants cute without a craft-store marathon. Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.

🎃 Pick My Costume
Pick my costume
Sports Arena
Sports Costume Ideas
Quick answer: start with the Soccer Squad (25 min; jerseys, black for the ref, one red card), the Basketball Star (5 min; jersey, eye-black stripes), or the Referee (20 min; striped shirt, whistle, yellow penalty flag). Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
All 8 Sports Arena costumes
Sports Arena is the competitive corner of the Costume Galaxy, with eight sports costumes for MVPs and their entourages. Soccer squads, basketball stars, boxers, referees, and cheer crews live here, built mostly from real jerseys and gear you already own. It is the fastest region in the galaxy, and most builds take twenty-five minutes or less, because the uniform does the talking. It suits young athletes, friend groups who want a theme, and the famously reluctant dresser who will wear a jersey but not a costume. Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
Soccer Squad 25 min · Easy
Basketball Star 5 min · Easy
Referee 20 min · Easy
Boxer 10 min · Easy

🎃 Pick My Costume

Pantry

🎃 Pick My Costume
Pick my costume
Pop Culture Plaza
Pop Culture Costume Ideas
Quick answer: start with the Mystery Crew (15 min; leader, style icon, brains, goofball, one good dog), the Goggle Crew (10 min; yellow tees, denim overalls, goggles), or the Neon Demon Hunter (25 min; streetwear, glowing sigils, foam sword). Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
All 32 Pop Culture Plaza costumes
Pop Culture Plaza is the main-character district of the Costume Galaxy, with thirty-two costumes from movies, memes, and games. Screen icons, viral memes, video game heroes, and music acts live here, from the Neon Demon Hunter to the Mystery Crew and the Goggle Crew. Builds range from thrift-store streetwear to cardboard props, and most come together in under forty-five minutes. It suits teens and adults who want to be recognized instantly, friend groups splitting a cast, and anyone whose costume references need no explanation. Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
Neon Demon Hunter 25 min · Easy

Pick my costume
Silly Street
Funny DIY Halloween Costumes
Quick answer: start with the Moth and Porch Light (40 min; cardboard wings / yellow and a lampshade), the Error 404 (10 min; all black, blank white page), or the Party Pinata (40 min; cardboard box, rainbow fringe). Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.
All 26 Silly Street costumes
Silly Street is the pure-comedy borough of the Costume Galaxy: twenty-six funny costumes with zero scares. The Moth and the Porch Light, Error 404, the Party Pinata, and a parade of pun builds live here, most of them cardboard, face paint, and thrift-store finds. Several go from idea to party-ready in about ten minutes, which makes this the last-minute lifeline of the galaxy. It suits class clowns, office costume contests, and anyone who would rather get the laugh than the fright. Every costume below links to a free step-by-step build guide.

## Page: https://pickmycostume.com/white-sheet-costumes

Pick My Costume
Pick

Pantry

Updated November 2026 · Pick My Costume
White Sheet Costume Ideas
That old bedsheet in the linen closet is the fastest costume in the house. A white flat sheet, scissors, and a marker get you the classic ghost in ten minutes flat, and a black sheet cut into a cape covers vampires, headless horsemen, and little witches with almost no sewing.
The trick most people miss is sizing the sheet before you cut: twin for kids under eight, full or queen for teens and adults, and always cut eye holes smaller than you think, you can widen them but you cannot shrink them.
Every costume below starts from a sheet you already own, lists exactly what else you need, gives the build steps right on this page, and links to a full build guide with real hands-on time. No costume-shop run required.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Classic Ghost
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 white flat sheet: twin size for kids under 8, full size for tweens and adults; Black marker, thick tip, 1; Scissors, 1 pair; 2 small squares of black tulle or sheer fabric, about 4 inches each (optional, for see-through eyes; buy: craft store).
A white sheet with cut-out eyes.
How to make it
Drape the sheet over the wearer and mark both eye spots.
Take the sheet off. Cut the holes small first, then widen a little at a time.
Draw a mouth, trim the hem so it clears the ground, and drape the sheet back on.
Build this costume →
Little Witch
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Black cape or black bedsheet, 1; Pointy witch hat, 1; Black-and-white striped tights, 1 pair; Green non-toxic face paint, 1 tube; Safety pin or ribbon, 1.
Black cape, pointy hat, striped tights, green face paint.
How to make it
Pin or tie the black cape at the shoulders, loose at the neck.
Paint the nose, chin, and forehead lightly green. Use non-toxic face paint only, and keep it clear of the eyes.
Pull on the striped tights and the pointy hat.
Build this costume →
Headless Horsemen
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: Black cape or black sheet, 1 per person; Small jack-o-lantern bucket or foam pumpkin, 1 per person; Broom or stick-horse substitute, 1 per person; Tape, 1 roll; Glow bracelets, 1 pack.
Black capes, jack-o-lanterns held at shoulder height, group gallop.
How to make it
Drape the black cape over the shoulders and tuck the chin low, so you can still see the ground.
Hold the pumpkin bucket up at shoulder height, like a carried head.
Add glow bracelets so drivers can see you, and gallop in a group line.
Build this costume →
Coffee Cup
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: White trash bag or white sheet, 1 large; Cardboard tube or large cylinder, 1; Brown paper or felt for the lid, 1 sheet; Brown marker, 1 thick.
White trash bag over a cardboard tube, brown lid hat.
How to make it
Cut the head and arm holes in the white bag or sheet. Cut the head hole wide enough to see and breathe with ease, and wear it over clothes.
Draw a coffee shop logo on the front with the brown marker.
Cut a brown paper circle as the lid hat, and wear it on top.
Build this costume →
Classic Vampire
⏱ 25 min hands-on Easy
You need: Black cape or black bedsheet, 1; Black shirt and pants, 1 set; Plastic vampire fangs, 1 pair; Hair gel or pomade, 1; Red lipstick or red face paint, 1; White face powder or pale face paint, 1.
Black cape, fangs, slicked hair.
How to make it
Dress in black, and slick the hair straight back with gel.
Dust pale paint over the face, and add a thin red line at each corner of the mouth.
Wear the black cape, and pop the fangs in last. Skip the fangs for small kids.
Build this costume →
Caped Duo
⏱ 30 min hands-on Easy
You need: 2 old twin sheets or large fabric rectangles, about 4x5 feet each; Craft felt for masks and emblems, 2 sheets 9x12 inches; Ribbon or cord for cape ties, about 3 feet per cape; Fabric glue, 1 tube; Paper and pencil for sketching, 1 set; Scissors, 1 pair.
Matching sheet capes, felt masks, and your own emblems.
How to make it
Cut each sheet into a cape.
Cut felt emblems and eye masks. Glue one emblem to the back of each cape.
Tie the capes in a loose bow that pulls free easily, and put the masks on.
Build this costume →
Dino Herd
⏱ 30 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 green poncho or green bedsheet per person, about 50x60 inches; 1 sheet green felt per person, 9x12 inches; 1 old sock per person, white or colored; Scrap fabric or cotton balls for stuffing, about 1 cup per person; Fabric glue, 1 tube, or 6 safety pins per person; Scissors, 1 pair.
Green ponchos with felt spikes and stuffed-sock tails.
How to make it
Cut 8 to 10 felt triangles, all from one paper template.
Pin the triangles in a row down the back of the green poncho.
Stuff an old sock, and pin it to the back waistband as the tail.
Build this costume →
Pixel Ghost
⏱ 30 min hands-on Easy
You need: White bedsheet or white fabric, 1 twin-size; Black felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches; Fabric glue, 1 tube; Scissors, 1 pair; Marker and ruler, 1 each.
A white sheet cut in chunky pixel squares with felt eyes.
How to make it
Cut the bottom edge of the sheet into chunky square zigzags, about 4 inches each.
Draw two square eyes and a square mouth on the black felt, cut them out, and glue them onto the top third of the sheet.
Press the felt pieces down firmly, one at a time. Drape the sheet on over dark clothes, with the eye area kept open.
Build this costume →
Sushi Roll
⏱ 40 min hands-on Easy
You need: White bedsheet or large white t-shirt to wear, 1; Dark green felt, 1 large sheet; Pink or orange felt, 1 large sheet; White pom-poms, 4 large, plus 1 green pom-pom; Toy chopsticks, 1 pair, or 2 wooden sticks; Fabric glue, 1 bottle; Scissors, 1 pair.
A white-sheet wrap with felt salmon and pom-pom wasabi. Chopsticks optional.
How to make it
Dress in the white sheet or large white t-shirt.
Cut the dark green felt into a wide band, and glue or pin it around the waist as the seaweed wrap.
Glue pink felt strips across the front as salmon, and add pom-pom rice and one green pom-pom as wasabi.
Build this costume →
The Doctor & the Bride
⏱ 25 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 old dark suit or jacket; Green face paint, non-toxic, 1 tube; 2 plastic neck bolts, costume style; 1 white dress or old white sheet; White hair spray, 1 can; Tape, 1 roll or glue, 1 bottle; Scissors, 1 pair; Dark eye shadow, 1.
Green face paint and neck bolts for one; tall streaked wig and torn gown for the other.
How to make it
The Doctor: paint the face and neck green, and tape the two bolts to the sides of the neck. Keep paint away from the eyes, and patch-test first.
The Bride: put on the white dress, and tear the bottom hem into strips by hand, starting small.
Smudge dark eye shadow under the eyes. Spray in the white hair streak last.
Build this costume →
🔔 One email on Oct 27
Want one email on Oct 27 with costumes you can make that night? That’s it, one email, then you’re off the list.
Remind me
Questions, answered
What size sheet should I use? Twin for kids under eight, full or queen for teens and adults. A sheet that is too big drags on the ground and trips the wearer. You can always trim a sheet, you cannot add fabric back.
How do I keep a sheet ghost costume from slipping? Cut eye holes smaller than you think first; you can widen them but not shrink them. A tied sash or belt at the waist holds the sheet in place, and safety pins at the shoulders stop it sliding on kids.
Do I need to sew anything? No. Every costume on this page is no-sew. Cut sheet edges do not fray enough to matter for one night, and tape or pins handle the rest.
Can my child actually see through the eye holes? Yes, if you place them right. Have the wearer put the sheet on first, mark the eye spots with a washable marker while they look straight ahead, then cut. Cut small, test, then widen.
Own the supplies already? Check the Pantry to see which of all 169 costumes you can make tonight from what is in your house. Or wander the costume galaxy .
Can’t decide? Pick my costume : the 2-minute quiz that picks your top 3.

## Page: https://pickmycostume.com/cardboard-box-costumes

Pick My Costume

Updated November 2026 · Pick My Costume
Cardboard Box Costume Ideas
The box your last delivery came in is a costume waiting to happen. A medium box worn over the torso becomes a robot, a pizza slice, a game block, or a dinosaur body with nothing more than a box cutter, tape, and paint.
Ask a grocery or liquor store for spares if you need big ones, they give them away free most mornings. Cut arm and head holes smaller than you think, reinforce inside edges with packing tape so they survive the night, and keep paint to one or two coats so the cardboard stays light.
Every costume below starts from a box, lists the rest of the supplies honestly, and links to a full build guide with real hands-on time. The box is already in the recycling. The costume is not far behind.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Copy these costumes
Pizza Slice
⏱ 45 min hands-on Medium
You need: Large cardboard box, 1; Yellow and orange acrylic paint, 1 bottle each; Red felt, 1 sheet; Brown felt scraps for crust, or 1 brown paper bag; Paintbrush, scissors, tape, 1 set; Fabric glue, 1 tube.
A big cardboard triangle, painted golden with felt pepperoni.
How to make it
Cut a big triangle from the cardboard, about 3 feet tall.
Paint it golden yellow-orange. An adult cuts red felt circles, and you glue them on spread out as pepperoni.
Glue a brown crust strip along the wide end, tape two string loops to the back, and wear it like a sandwich board, crust at the top.
Build this costume →
Donut
⏱ 35 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 large cardboard box, about 24x24 inches flat; Pink paint, 1 small bottle; Felt sprinkles, 12 to 15 small pieces, or sticker sprinkles; Ribbon or string, 4 feet; Scissors, 1 pair and glue, 1 bottle.
Pink cardboard ring with sprinkles, worn like a sandwich board.
How to make it
Draw a big circle on the cardboard, about 30 inches across. Cut the center hole smaller than the head first, then widen it slowly, keeping fingers clear of the scissors.
Paint the ring pink.
Glue on felt or sticker sprinkles, attach ribbon at the top, and wear it like a sandwich board.
Build this costume →
Kart Racers
⏱ 45 min hands-on Medium
You need: Large cardboard box, 1 per racer, big enough to fit around the torso; Red, blue, green, and yellow paint or wrapping paper, 1 bottle or roll per color; Paper plates for wheels, 4 per kart; Racing cap or helmet, 1 per person; Scissors, 1 pair, tape, 1 roll, and string, 1 spool; Ribbon for kart straps, about 3 feet per kart.
Cardboard karts and racing caps for a full starting grid of friends.
How to make it
Have each racer step into their box and mark the waist before cutting. Cut the top and bottom out small first, then widen.
Paint each kart a different bright color, and tape two paper plate wheels to each side.
Tape ribbon straps inside so the kart hangs at waist height with legs free to move. Tape every cut edge smooth, and wear the kart with a racing cap.
Build this costume →
Ghost Hunters
⏱ 30 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 khaki or tan jumpsuit, or matching shirt and pants, per person; 1 small cardboard box per person, shoebox size; White paper, 2 sheets, and markers for name patches; 1 sheet black cardboard per person; Packing tape or glue, scissors.
Khaki jumpsuits, cardboard ghost-catching backpacks, name patches.
How to make it
Tape a small cardboard box shut for each backpack. An adult cuts the straps, dial, and hose from black cardboard.
Tape or glue those pieces onto the box.
Write each person's last name on white paper and tape it to the chest as a name patch. Wear the backpack over a khaki jumpsuit, and keep the box small and light.
Build this costume →
Popcorn Bucket
⏱ 30 min hands-on Easy
You need: Cardboard box, 1 medium; Red and white striped wrapping paper or paint, 1 roll; Yellow or white balloons, 8 to 10; Tape, string, scissors, 1 set; Red marker for the label, 1.
A striped cardboard-box body with balloon popcorn on top.
How to make it
An adult cuts the head and arm holes small first, then widens them to fit. Tape the inside edges so the cardboard does not scratch.
Cover the box with red and white stripes, using striped paper or paint, and add the label with the red marker.
Blow up the balloons and tie them in a cluster on top of the box, then step in. Keep balloons whole and away from toddlers.
Build this costume →
Block Game Crew
⏱ 45 min hands-on Medium
You need: 1 large cardboard box per person, big enough to fit over the torso; Acrylic paint in each hero's colors, 1 small bottle per color; Paintbrushes, 1 wide and 1 detail per person; Black marker, 1; Scissors, 1 pair.
Cardboard-box heads: pick your blocky hero.
How to make it
Each person picks a blocky game hero. An adult measures each head and cuts the head opening and eye holes wide, so everyone can see clearly.
Paint each box in that hero's main colors.
Draw a square face and details on the front with the black marker, and wear the boxes over regular clothes.
Build this costume →
Cardboard Robot Crew
⏱ 45 min hands-on Medium
You need: Medium cardboard box per person, 1 each; Small cardboard box per person for the head, 1 each; Aluminum foil, 1 large roll; Plastic bottle caps, about 20 total; Duct tape, 1 roll; Black permanent marker, 1; Elastic string or yarn, 6 feet; Glow sticks, 1 per person.
Boxy robots built from cardboard boxes, foil, and bottle-cap buttons.
How to make it
Cut head and arm holes in each big box, and wide eye holes in each small head box. Cut slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
Wrap every box in foil and tape it down. Draw dials on the chest, and tape bottle caps beside them as buttons.
Slide into the torso box and tie the head box on with the chin string loose. Tape a cracked glow stick to the chest as a power light.
Build this costume →
Plug and Socket
⏱ 45 min hands-on Easy
You need: Cardboard box, 1 large; Gray and white acrylic paint, 1 small bottle each; Black markers, 1 set; Craft foam, 1 sheet 9x12 inches; Tape, 1 roll, and string, 1 spool, for wearing; Scissors, 1 pair.
Cardboard plug and outlet worn front and back.
How to make it
Cut two cardboard panels, each about 2 feet square.
Paint one gray and add foam prongs for the plug. Paint the other white and draw dark slots for the socket.
Tape string to the back corners and hang the panels like signs. Never loop string around the neck.
Build this costume →
Haunted Animatronics
⏱ 60 min hands-on Medium
You need: 1 large cardboard box per person, big enough to cover the head; 2 red LED tea lights per person; Paint in gray, black, and one accent color, 1 small bottle each; 1 set old clothes with holes or tears; Hot glue gun, 1; scissors, 1 pair; utility knife, 1 (adults only).
Glitchy mascot heads from cardboard boxes, flickering LED eyes, jerky moves.
How to make it
An adult marks the eye holes and the wide jagged mouth, checks the eye spots while the wearer holds the box up, then cuts both wide. Cardboard cannot be put back.
Paint the box gray with black scuffs and cracks. An adult glues one red LED tea light inside each eye hole with the hot glue gun.
Wear the box over old clothes and move in short jerky steps. Walk with a partner who can see clearly, never wear the box near stairs or traffic, and take the box off if you feel hot.
Build this costume →
Party Pinata
⏱ 40 min hands-on Medium
You need: Cardboard box, 1 large; Crepe paper in rainbow colors, 6 rolls; Wrapped candy, 2 bags; String for hanging strips, 1 roll; Tape, 1 roll; Scissors, 1 pair.
A cardboard box wrapped in rainbow fringe, with real candy inside.
How to make it
Cut fringe strips from the crepe paper, and glue them in overlapping rows until the whole box is covered.
Cut arm and head holes, keeping the head hole generous so seeing and breathing stay easy. Leave an opening at the bottom.
Fill the box with wrapped candy only, seal the bottom flap loosely, and hand out candy from inside the costume all night.
Build this costume →
Fairy Tale Princesses
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 dress from the closet per person; 1 cereal box per crown; Gold or silver paint or markers, 1 set; Scissors, 1 pair and tape, 1 roll; 1 hair ribbon per person.
A dress or a crown from the closet. Every princess works.
How to make it
Each princess picks a dress from her own closet.
An adult draws a crown on a cereal box, checks the fit against the head, and cuts it out, leaving a 1 inch tab to tape the ends together.
Color the crown gold or silver, tape it on, and tie the hair ribbon in a bow under the crown.
Build this costume →
Good Witch, Bad Witch
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 black dress or set of black clothes for the bad witch; 1 pink dress or set of pink clothes for the good witch; Green face paint, non-toxic, 1 tube; 1 cardboard crown; 1 black cone hat; Hot glue gun, scissors, 1 pink marker, tape.
Green face paint and black for one, pink gown and crown for the other.
How to make it
Bad witch: wear black, and paint the face and hands green with non-toxic paint. Keep the paint away from the eyes, and patch test sensitive skin first.
An adult folds the black hat brim and hot glues it in place. Hot glue sets in seconds, so check the fit in a mirror first.
Good witch: wear pink, color the cardboard crown with the pink marker, and tape it on.
Build this costume →

Questions, answered
Where do I get big cardboard boxes for free? Ask grocery or liquor stores in the morning; they give away sturdy boxes free most days. Appliance boxes from a buy-nothing group are the best fit for kid torsos.
How do I stop the cardboard tearing at the arm holes? Reinforce every cut edge on the inside with packing tape before the costume goes on. Cut holes smaller than you think and widen slowly; cardboard cut away cannot go back.
What paint works on cardboard? Acrylic craft paint or spray paint, one or two thin coats. Thick coats add weight and make the box sag by the end of the night.
Is a cardboard box costume safe for little kids? Have an adult do all box-cutter work and tape every inside edge so raw cardboard never scratches skin. Keep the costume away from open flames; cardboard is flammable.

Updated November 2026 · Pick My Costume
No-Sew Costume Ideas
If you do not sew, you are not locked out of a good homemade costume. Most of the ideas below hold together with safety pins, fabric tape, hot glue, or nothing at all, just clothes arranged cleverly.
Pin from the inside so the backs never touch skin, use double-sided fabric tape for hems that need to look clean, and remember that a hot glue gun sets in under a minute, which beats waiting on stitches you were never going to do.
Every costume below needs no needle, lists exactly what to pull from the closet, gives the build steps right on this page, and links to a full build guide with real hands-on time. Thread not required.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Office Couple
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: White button-down shirts, 2; Name tags, 2; Toy teapot or a small real teapot, 1; Black pants or skirts, 2; Marker for writing names, 1.
White shirts, name tags, and a teapot. The office's finest.
How to make it
Write joke job titles on the name tags.
Pin the tags on white shirts, worn with black pants or skirts.
One person carries the teapot. The other carries a clipboard.
Build this costume →
Lost Tourist
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: Button-down shirt, 1; Sunglasses and camera or phone on a strap, 1 set; Paper map, 1; Luggage tag, 1; Clear tape, 1 roll.
Wear wrinkled clothes, carry a crumpled map, add one luggage tag backwards on your shoulder.
How to make it
Wrinkle the shirt on purpose and put the sunglasses on top of your head.
Tape a luggage tag backwards on one shoulder.
Carry a paper map upside down, and hold it that way.
Build this costume →
Ninja
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: All-black outfit: t-shirt, pants, and a black beanie, 1 set; Black belt or sash, 1; Black headband or strip of black t-shirt, 1 strip about 3 inches wide; Scissors, 1 pair, and tape, 1 roll; Black non-toxic face paint for a mask stripe, 1 tube.
All black with a belt sash and a slit headband.
How to make it
Dress all in black and tie the sash around the waist.
Wrap the black strip around the forehead, with eyes and mouth uncovered.
Paint a thin black stripe across the nose if you like.
Build this costume →
Cereal Crew
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: Solid-color shirt and pants per person, 1 set each; Empty cereal boxes, 1 per person; Markers or crayons in assorted colors, 1 pack; String, about 4 feet per person; Scissors, 1 pair; Tape, 1 roll.
Solid-color clothes plus a cereal-box front you decorate.
How to make it
Cut the front panel off an empty cereal box.
Decorate it with a made-up cereal name and mascot.
Tape string to the top corners and wear the panel like a sign.
Build this costume →
Breakfast Buffet
⏱ 25 min hands-on Easy
You need: Cardboard sheets, 1 per person about 2x2 feet; Markers in assorted colors, 1 pack; String or yarn, about 4 feet per person; Scissors, 1 pair.
Everyone picks a breakfast: egg, bacon, toast, pancake, OJ, coffee. Cardboard signs over normal clothes.
How to make it
Cut a large circle or rectangle from the cardboard.
Draw your breakfast food big, filling the whole board.
Thread string through the top holes and wear it over normal clothes.
Build this costume →
Crowd Camouflage
⏱ 5 min hands-on Easy
You need: Gray hoodie, 1; Dark pants, 1 pair; Gray beanie, 1; Blank adhesive name tag, 1; Pen, 1.
Gray hoodie, dark pants, blank expression. Vanish into any crowd.
How to make it
Put on the gray hoodie, dark pants, and gray beanie.
Stick the blank name tag on your chest. Write nothing on it.
Keep a blank face and blend into the back of group photos.
Build this costume →
Bowling Pins
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: White shirt and pants per pin person, 1 set each; Red duct or electrical tape, 1 roll; Black shirt and pants for the bowler, 1 set; Toy bowling ball or black playground ball, 1; Scissors, 1 pair.
White outfits with red neck stripes, plus one bowler in black.
How to make it
Wrap two red tape stripes around the collar of the white shirt.
Wrap one stripe around each wrist.
The bowler dresses in black and carries a toy ball, never a real one.
Build this costume →
Salt & Pepper
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: White shirt, pants, and hat for Salt, 1 set; Black shirt, pants, and hat for Pepper, 1 set; Cardboard for 2 shaker tops; Gray paint or gray marker, 1; Black marker for the S and P, 1; Tape or glue, 1.
White and black outfits with shaker tops made from cardboard.
How to make it
Salt dresses all in white. Pepper dresses all in black.
Cut cardboard shaker tops, paint them gray, and dot holes on top.
Tape one top to each hat, with a big S on Salt and a big P on Pepper.
Build this costume →
Headless Horsemen
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: Black cape or black sheet, 1 per person; Small jack-o-lantern bucket or foam pumpkin, 1 per person; Broom or stick-horse substitute, 1 per person; Tape, 1 roll; Glow bracelets, 1 pack.
Black capes, jack-o-lanterns held at shoulder height, group gallop.
How to make it
Drape the black cape over the shoulders and tuck the chin low, so you can still see the ground.
Hold the pumpkin bucket up at shoulder height, like a carried head.
Add glow bracelets so drivers can see you, and gallop in a group line.
Build this costume →
Bacon & Eggs
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: Dark red or brown shirt for the bacon, 1; White shirt for the egg, 1; 1 sheet red-brown craft felt, 9x12 inches; 1 sheet each white and yellow craft felt, 9x12 inches; Safety pins, 6 to 8; Scissors, 1 pair.
Wavy bacon stripes and a sunny-side-up egg yolk.
How to make it
Cut wavy strips from the red-brown felt for the bacon.
Cut one large white oval and one yellow circle for the egg.
Pin the felt to the shirts from the inside, so pin backs face cloth, not skin.
Build this costume →
Penguin Huddle
⏱ 35 min hands-on Easy
You need: Black long-sleeve shirts, 1 per person; White felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches per person; Orange felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches per person; Headbands, 1 per person; Fabric glue, 1 tube; Scissors, 1 pair.
Black shirts, felt bellies, beak headbands. Waddle together.
How to make it
Cut a white felt belly and glue it to the front of the black shirt.
Glue an orange felt beak to the front of a headband.
Put on the shirt and headband, and waddle shoulder to shoulder.
Build this costume →
Plug and Socket
⏱ 45 min hands-on Easy
You need: Cardboard box, 1 large; Gray and white acrylic paint, 1 small bottle each; Black markers, 1 set; Craft foam, 1 sheet 9x12 inches; Tape, 1 roll, and string, 1 spool, for wearing; Scissors, 1 pair.
Cardboard plug and outlet worn front and back.
How to make it
Cut two cardboard panels, each about 2 feet square.
Paint one gray and add foam prongs for the plug. Paint the other white and draw dark slots for the socket.
Tape string to the back corners and hang the panels like signs. Never loop string around the neck.
Build this costume →

Questions, answered
What holds a no-sew costume together best? Double-sided fabric tape for hems that need to look clean, safety pins from the inside so the backs never touch skin, and a hot glue gun for anything rigid. Hot glue sets in under a minute.
Will safety pins show? Not if you pin from the inside of the garment. Pin through a seam or hem where the fabric is doubled so the pin has something to bite.
Can I wash clothes after using fabric tape or hot glue? Fabric tape usually survives a gentle wash. Hot glue peels off most fabrics if you pick at an edge. Test a hidden spot first on clothes you care about.

Quick answer: Classic Ghost (10 min), Emoji Crew (15 min), Basketball Star (5 min): all buildable tonight in 30 minutes or less of hands-on work. Tap any name for its full build guide: materials list, numbered steps, and safety notes.
It is the night of the party and you have nothing. Every costume below takes 30 minutes or less of hands-on work, and total time stays under two hours, so you can start after dinner and finish before bed. The two marked No shopping need nothing beyond basic household items; the rest may need a quick store run. Have more than the basics at home? Tick what you own and more tonight options unlock.

Remind me
Questions, answered
What is the one rule for last-minute costumes? One hero piece. A ghost needs only the sheet, a tourist needs only the camera and socks-with-sandals. Build around a single recognizable item and let closet clothes do the rest.
What should I skip when time is short? Anything that has to dry: paint, glue-heavy builds, papier-mache. A hair dryer buys you minutes, not miracles.
How do I not look like I gave up? Commit to the bit. A name tag, a prop, or a one-line character voice sells a simple costume more than extra accessories do.
Still deciding? Pick my costume : five quick questions, three picks matched to you. Or check the Pantry to see which costumes you can make from what is in your house.
See all last-minute costumes

## Page: https://pickmycostume.com/family-costumes

Pick My Costume

Updated November 2026 · Pick My Costume
Family Halloween Costume Ideas
A family costume only works if the littlest member can actually wear it, sit in it, and survive the evening in it.
The sets below were picked because every member gets a real costume, not a background role, and the builds scale: make the baby the centerpiece, give the teens the funny parts, and keep total build time sane by repeating one simple base across the group. Start with the hardest costume first, usually the smallest person, and fit everything while they are still in a good mood.
Every set below links to full build guides with real hands-on time per person, so there are no day-of surprises.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Goggle Crew
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 yellow t-shirt per person; 1 pair denim overalls per person; 1 pair swim or safety goggles per person; 1 pair black gloves per person.
Yellow tees, denim overalls, goggles, black gloves.
How to make it
Each person puts on a yellow t-shirt, denim overalls, and black gloves.
Push the goggles up on the forehead, never over the eyes, so everyone can see clearly.
Walk in a pack, and greet people in gibberish. Skip any real tools or hard hats.
Build this costume →
Classic Ghost
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 white flat sheet: twin size for kids under 8, full size for tweens and adults; Black marker, thick tip, 1; Scissors, 1 pair; 2 small squares of black tulle or sheer fabric, about 4 inches each (optional, for see-through eyes; buy: craft store).
A white sheet with cut-out eyes.
How to make it
Drape the sheet over the wearer and mark both eye spots.
Take the sheet off. Cut the holes small first, then widen a little at a time.
Draw a mouth, trim the hem so it clears the ground, and drape the sheet back on.
Build this costume →
Emoji Crew
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 yellow t-shirt per person; 1 large white paper plate, 10-inch, or cardboard circle per person; Markers in black, red, and blue, 1 set; Scissors, 1 pair and tape, 1 roll.
Everyone picks an emoji: a yellow tee plus a big printed face.
How to make it
Everyone picks an emoji, and puts on a yellow t-shirt.
Draw the emoji on a paper plate in pencil first, then go over it with the markers. An adult handles the scissors when trimming the plate.
Tape the plate flat to the chest of the shirt, and gather the crew in a row for photos.
Build this costume →
Dino Rangers
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Khaki shirt, 1, and khaki pants, 1 pair, per grown-up; Green hoodie per child, 1 each; White paper or card, 2 sheets; 1 toy dinosaur or plush per kid; Ribbon or string, 18 inches per kid; Tape, 1 roll and scissors, 1 pair.
Khaki outfits for the grown-ups, dino hoods for the kids. Leash a toy raptor.
How to make it
Grown-ups dress in khaki shirts and pants, with the sleeves rolled. Each kid wears a green hoodie.
An adult draws two oval eye spots on white paper, checks them against the hood, and cuts them out. Tape the spots to the hood.
Loop the ribbon around a toy dinosaur like a leash, and tie the other end to the kid's wrist, keeping the leash short. Skip small plastic dinosaur toys for kids under three, since they are a choking hazard.
Build this costume →
Bowling Pins
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: White shirt and pants per pin person, 1 set each; Red duct or electrical tape, 1 roll; Black shirt and pants for the bowler, 1 set; Toy bowling ball or black playground ball, 1; Scissors, 1 pair.
White outfits with red neck stripes, plus one bowler in black.
How to make it
Wrap two red tape stripes around the collar of the white shirt.
Wrap one stripe around each wrist.
The bowler dresses in black and carries a toy ball, never a real one.
Build this costume →
Mystery Crew
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Orange, purple, blue, and red t-shirts, 1 each; Dog ears headband or a brown dog costume piece, 1; Fake magnifying glass, 1; Headband or scarf in a matching color, 1 per person; Brown non-toxic face paint for the dog's nose, 1 tube.
Assign the leader, the style icon, the brains, the goofball, and one very good dog.
How to make it
Assign the roles: orange for the leader, purple for the style icon, blue for the brains, red for the goofball. The dog wears the ears headband.
Each person puts on their color t-shirt and a matching headband or scarf, tied loose, never tight. The brains carries the fake magnifying glass.
Paint a brown nose on the dog with non-toxic face paint, keeping it clear of the eyes. Line up with the dog in front, and point at something suspicious.
Build this costume →
Fairy Tale Princesses
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 dress from the closet per person; 1 cereal box per crown; Gold or silver paint or markers, 1 set; Scissors, 1 pair and tape, 1 roll; 1 hair ribbon per person.
A dress or a crown from the closet. Every princess works.
How to make it
Each princess picks a dress from her own closet.
An adult draws a crown on a cereal box, checks the fit against the head, and cuts it out, leaving a 1 inch tab to tape the ends together.
Color the crown gold or silver, tape it on, and tie the hair ribbon in a bow under the crown.
Build this costume →
Plumber Duo
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Blue overalls, 2; Red t-shirt and green t-shirt, 1 each; Red cap and green cap, 1 each; Brown non-toxic face paint for mustaches, 1 tube; White circle stickers or white paper, 2 about 2 inches across; Marker, 1.
Overalls, red and green caps and shirts, drawn mustaches.
How to make it
Write a big M on one white circle and an L on the other, and stick or tape them to the red cap and the green cap.
Each brother wears blue overalls over their colored t-shirt and cap.
Paint on the mustaches with brown non-toxic face paint: a big bushy one for red, a thinner one for green. Keep the paint clear of the eyes, and test it on skin first.
Build this costume →
Cereal Crew
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: Solid-color shirt and pants per person, 1 set each; Empty cereal boxes, 1 per person; Markers or crayons in assorted colors, 1 pack; String, about 4 feet per person; Scissors, 1 pair; Tape, 1 roll.
Solid-color clothes plus a cereal-box front you decorate.
How to make it
Cut the front panel off an empty cereal box.
Decorate it with a made-up cereal name and mascot.
Tape string to the top corners and wear the panel like a sign.
Build this costume →
Decades Crew
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: Each person's own closet clothes; 1 printed decade card per person, e.g. 70s, 80s, 90s, cardstock or paper; Scissors, 1 pair; Tape, 1 roll or safety pins, 1 pack; Hair gel or spray, 1.
Each person picks a decade and dresses from their own closet.
How to make it
Everyone picks a different decade, and builds the look from their own closet: bell bottoms and a headband for the 70s, neon and high socks for the 80s, flannel tied at the waist for the 90s.
Letter each decade card big, with letters at least 4 inches tall, and tape one card to each chest. An adult handles the scissors when trimming the cards.
Style the hair with gel to match the decade, and keep props light so the looks last all night.
Build this costume →
Mermaid Crew
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: T-shirt or dress in a sea color (teal, purple, red, white), 1 per person; Face paint in a matching accent color, 1 tube; Plastic trident prop, 1; Toy crab or red paper for a cardboard crab, 1; Shell necklace, 1; Scissors and tape, 1 set.
The mermaid, the prince, the sea king, the sea witch, or the crab: pick your role.
How to make it
Sketch the cheek detail on paper first, then paint one small detail on each person: scales, a seaweed swirl, or an anchor. Keep the face paint clear of the eyes.
Cut a red paper crab body, legs, and claws slowly, and tape them to the smallest person's shirt, or hand them the toy crab instead.
The sea king carries the plastic trident. Everyone else picks one accessory, like the shell necklace, and stands tall for the crew photo.
Build this costume →
Fruit Salad Crew
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: Solid-color outfits in fruit colors (red, yellow, green, orange), 1 set per person; Green felt for leaf hats, 1 sheet 9x12 inches per person; Headbands, 1 per person; Fabric glue, 1 tube.
Each person picks a fruit color, wears it head to toe with a leaf hat.
How to make it
Each person picks a fruit, and wears that color head to toe.
An adult cuts leaf shapes from the green felt, keeping fingers clear of the scissors.
Glue one leaf to each headband and press it down firmly. Wear the headbands, and take the fruit salad group photo.

Remind me
Questions, answered
Which family member's costume should we build first? The smallest. Fit the toddler or baby while they are still in a good mood, then scale the adult versions off the same simple base.
Do we all have to match exactly? No. One repeated color, hat, or prop reads as a group in photos. Matching exactly multiplies the work; a shared element is enough.
How do we keep total build time sane? Repeat one simple base across the group instead of building six different costumes. Assembly-line the repeated piece, then add one distinguishing detail per person.
