Updated November 2026 · Pick My Costume
Couples Halloween Costume Ideas
The best couples costumes have a joke a stranger gets in three seconds: ketchup and mustard, plug and socket, sun and moon.
Pick the one where both people are equally recognizable, nobody wants to be the human accessory. Build both halves side by side so the colors and sizes match, and agree in advance on the effort level, one elaborate half next to one thrown-together half reads as a mistake, not a duo.
Every pair below links to full build guides with real hands-on time, so you both know what the evening is going to take.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Office Couple
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: White button-down shirts, 2; Name tags, 2; Toy teapot or a small real teapot, 1; Black pants or skirts, 2; Marker for writing names, 1.
White shirts, name tags, and a teapot. The office's finest.
How to make it
Write joke job titles on the name tags.
Pin the tags on white shirts, worn with black pants or skirts.
One person carries the teapot. The other carries a clipboard.
Build this costume →
Galaxy Knights
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 brown or beige bathrobe or long coat per knight; 1 toy energy-blade prop per knight; 1 wide belt or rope sash per knight; 1 pair dark pants and boots per knight; Brown face paint for a hood shadow, 1 tube, optional.
Robes, belts, and toy energy blades for knights of a far-off galaxy.
How to make it
Wear the bathrobe over dark pants and boots, and tie the belt or sash at the waist.
Pull the hood up, and carry the toy energy blade unlit until the photo.
Keep toy blades pointed up or down, never at faces, and keep any sparring slow and pretend. Light the blades for the council photo.
Build this costume →
Prince & Princess
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: Gold paper crown or plastic crown, 1; Cape or long piece of fabric, 1 about 3 feet long; Thrifted gown or long dress, 1; Tiara, 1; Toy scepter or wand, 1.
A crown and cape, a thrifted gown and tiara.
How to make it
The prince wears the gold crown and the cape over dark clothes, and carries the toy scepter. Keep the cape above the knees, and keep the neck tie loose so it pulls free easily.
The princess wears the thrifted gown and the tiara.
Walk in with royal posture, wave slowly with a bent wrist, and call everyone my good subject.
Build this costume →
Burger Joint Couple
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: 2 white aprons; Fake mustache, 1; Curly red wig, 1; Costume glasses, 1 pair; Order pad and pencil, 1 set.
White apron plus fake mustache, curly red wig plus glasses. Burger shop owners.
How to make it
One partner pulls on a white apron and sticks on the fake mustache with its skin-safe adhesive. Test the spot in a mirror first.
The other partner pulls on the second apron, the curly red wig, and the costume glasses.
Carry the order pad and pencil, and take each other's orders all night. Take the mustache off gently at the end of the night.
Build this costume →
Ketchup & Mustard
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 red t-shirt, 1 yellow t-shirt; Red felt or construction paper, 1 sheet 9x12 inches; Yellow felt or construction paper, 1 sheet 9x12 inches; Safety pins, 8; Scissors, 1 pair.
Red bottle tunic and cap for one, yellow for the other.
How to make it
Pick who is ketchup and who is mustard. Cut a big blob shape from the red paper and a matching one from the yellow paper, each about dinner plate size.
Pin the red blob to the yellow shirt and the yellow blob to the red shirt, so each person wears the other one's color. That is the joke.
Use 4 safety pins each, pinned from inside the shirt so no pin backs touch skin.
Build this costume →
Salt & Pepper
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: White shirt, pants, and hat for Salt, 1 set; Black shirt, pants, and hat for Pepper, 1 set; Cardboard for 2 shaker tops; Gray paint or gray marker, 1; Black marker for the S and P, 1; Tape or glue, 1.
White and black outfits with shaker tops made from cardboard.
How to make it
Salt dresses all in white. Pepper dresses all in black.
Cut cardboard shaker tops, paint them gray, and dot holes on top.
Tape one top to each hat, with a big S on Salt and a big P on Pepper.
Build this costume →
Cat & Mouse
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: 2 headbands; 1 sheet black craft felt, 9x12 inches; 1 sheet gray craft felt, 9x12 inches; Black eyeliner pencil or non-toxic face paint, 1; Scissors, 1 pair; Tape, 1 roll; Pink felt, 1 small triangle (optional, for inner ears; buy: craft store).
Cat ears versus mouse ears. Spend the night chasing each other.
How to make it
Cut a paper ear first to test the size: triangles for the cat, rounds for the mouse. Then cut two triangle ears from the black felt and two round ears from the gray felt.
Tape one pair of ears to each headband, and put the headbands on.
Draw whiskers on both faces with the eyeliner pencil, keeping the eyeliner clear of the eyes. Spend the night chasing each other.

Head-to-toe pink outfits with plastic accessories for the dream crew.

Wear an all-pink outfit head to toe, with the pink sunglasses.
Add one plastic accessory each, like a tiara, a handbag, or a toy phone.
Drape the feather boa over whoever feels the most plastic today, and strike the wave and smile pose.

Player One & Two

Matching tees with 1 and 2, toy controllers in hand, ready for co-op.
How to make it
Pin or tape the letters to the shirts first, and check them in a mirror. Ironed letters cannot be moved.
An adult irons a big 1 on the front and back of one t-shirt and a big 2 on the other, or draw the numbers with fabric markers instead.
Each player wears their numbered shirt and carries a toy controller. Walk in together, controllers up.

Peanut Butter & Jelly
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: Brown t-shirt, 1; Purple t-shirt, 1; White poster board, 2 sheets; Markers, 1 set; Scissors, 1 pair, and tape or string, 1 roll or spool.
One in brown with a PB label, one in purple with a J label.
How to make it
Draw a bread shape on the poster board, and hold it against a t-shirt to check the size. Cut two big bread shapes, cutting slowly and keeping fingers clear of the scissors.
Write PB in big letters on one shape and J on the other.
Tape or string the PB sign to the front of the brown t-shirt and the J sign to the purple one. Stand pressed together, bread sides out.

Questions, answered
What makes a couples costume actually work? A joke a stranger gets in three seconds: ketchup and mustard, plug and socket, sun and moon. If you have to explain it, pick a different pair.
How do we avoid one person being the boring half? Pick the pair where both halves are equally recognizable, and agree on the effort level in advance. One elaborate half next to a thrown-together half reads as a mistake, not a duo.
We waited until the last minute. What still works? Pairs built from closet clothes: office couple, salt and pepper, cat and mouse. Build both halves side by side so the colors and sizes match.

Updated November 2026 · Pick My Costume
Toddler Halloween Costume Ideas
Dressing a toddler is a different sport. Nothing itchy, nothing that covers the face, nothing with small parts, and it has to survive the stroller, the car seat, and a meltdown.
The costumes below were picked because they go over normal warm clothes, use soft materials, and take under half an hour, since toddlers do not do fittings. Do the fiddly bits while they nap and save the five-minute dress-up for right before you leave.
Every costume below links to a full build guide with real hands-on time and sizing notes for little bodies.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Ninja
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: All-black outfit: t-shirt, pants, and a black beanie, 1 set; Black belt or sash, 1; Black headband or strip of black t-shirt, 1 strip about 3 inches wide; Scissors, 1 pair, and tape, 1 roll; Black non-toxic face paint for a mask stripe, 1 tube.
All black with a belt sash and a slit headband.
How to make it
Dress all in black and tie the sash around the waist.
Wrap the black strip around the forehead, with eyes and mouth uncovered.
Paint a thin black stripe across the nose if you like.
Build this costume →
Ice Skater
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: White dress, 1; White tights, 1 pair; Hair donut for the bun, 1; Blush, 1; Bobby pins, 1 pack.
A white dress, tights, and a perfect bun: gold-medal energy, no ice required.
How to make it
Twist the hair into a high bun around the hair donut, and pin it in place.
Dab a little blush on the cheeks.
Wear the white dress with the white tights, and strike the finishing pose. Skip real skates: this costume is for dry land only.
Build this costume →
Classic Ghost
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 white flat sheet: twin size for kids under 8, full size for tweens and adults; Black marker, thick tip, 1; Scissors, 1 pair; 2 small squares of black tulle or sheer fabric, about 4 inches each (optional, for see-through eyes; buy: craft store).
A white sheet with cut-out eyes.
For under-3s: cut the sheet as a poncho with the face open. Never cover a toddler's face.
How to make it
Drape the sheet over the wearer and mark both eye spots.
Take the sheet off. Cut the holes small first, then widen a little at a time.
Draw a mouth, trim the hem so it clears the ground, and drape the sheet back on.
Build this costume →
Banana
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: Yellow sweatshirt and sweatpants, 1 set; Green felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches; Headband, 1; Fabric glue, 1 tube.
Yellow sweatsuit with a green felt stem hat.
How to make it
Put on the yellow sweatshirt and sweatpants.
An adult cuts a stem shape from the green felt, about 4 inches tall, keeping fingers clear of the scissors.
Glue the stem to the headband, check it in a mirror, and wear the headband.
Build this costume →
Backyard Superhero
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Old pillowcase or t-shirt for the cape, 1; Solid-color t-shirt to wear, 1; Cardstock or foam letter for the first initial, 1 sheet; Ribbon or string for cape ties, about 2 feet; Safety pins, 2; Scissors, 1 pair.
Short cape plus a first initial on the chest, mask optional.
How to make it
Hold the pillowcase against the back, mark waist length, and cut the cape. Keep it above the knees, and trim it after a fitting.
Cut the first initial from the cardstock, and pin it to the chest of the t-shirt.
Thread the ribbon through the top corners of the cape, and tie it at the neck in a loose bow that pulls free easily. Never tie anything tight around the neck.
Build this costume →
Cheerleader
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Team-color t-shirt and skirt or shorts, 1 set; 4 to 6 white plastic grocery bags; Hair ribbon in a team color, 1; Rubber bands or tape, 1 pack; Scissors, 1 pair.
Team colors and pom-poms made from cut plastic bags.
How to make it
An adult cuts the plastic bags into long strips right away, stopping 3 inches from one end. Never cut all the way through, and keep whole bags away from very small children.
Roll the uncut end tightly, wrap it with a rubber band or tape, and fluff the strips. Make a second pom-pom the same way.
Wear the team-color t-shirt and skirt or shorts, tie the hair ribbon in a bow, and carry a pom-pom in each hand.
Build this costume →
Pop Star
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Sparkly or sequin jacket, 1; Toy microphone, 1; Hair teasing comb, 1; Sunglasses, 1 pair; Dark jeans and a dark top, 1 set.
A sparkly jacket, a toy microphone, and the biggest hair in the room.
How to make it
Tease the hair big with the comb, going easy near the scalp, with no hard pulling.
Wear the sparkly jacket over the dark jeans and top, and put on the sunglasses.
Carry the toy microphone everywhere, and take requests.
Build this costume →
Little Baker
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: White paper or poster board for the hat, 2 sheets; Apron, 1; Toy whisk, 1; Flour from the kitchen, 1 pinch (optional, for the effect); Tape, 1 roll; Scissors, 1.
A paper chef hat, an apron, and a toy whisk.
How to make it
Roll the white paper into a tall chef hat, and tape the seam. Measure the head with a paper strip first, and trim the band to fit snug, so it does not slide over the eyes.
Wear the hat and the apron, and carry the toy whisk.
Offer everyone imaginary cupcakes. Keep real flour away from the eyes: a tiny pinch on the apron only.
Build this costume →
Cupcake
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Brown t-shirt or tunic for the wrapper, 1; White pillowcase for the frosting, 1; Red pom-pom or ball for the cherry, 1 about 2 inches; Fabric glue, 1 tube.
Brown tunic for the wrapper, white pillowcase for frosting, cherry on top.
How to make it
Put on the brown shirt. Drape the white pillowcase over the head and shoulders, and mark where the eyes are while wearing it.
Take the pillowcase off, and cut the eye holes small first, then widen them. Cut them wide: your child must see and breathe with ease.
Cut the bottom edge in waves, glue the red pom-pom on top as the cherry, and fluff the edges like frosting swirls.
Build this costume →

You need: 1 dress from the closet per person; 1 cereal box per crown; Gold or silver paint or markers, 1 set; Scissors, 1 pair and tape, 1 roll; 1 hair ribbon per person.
A dress or a crown from the closet. Every princess works.

Each princess picks a dress from her own closet.

Color the crown gold or silver, tape it on, and tie the hair ribbon in a bow under the crown.

Little Artist
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Beret or flat cap, 1; Cardboard for the palette, 1 piece; Washable paint set, 1; Old smock or oversized t-shirt, 1; Paintbrush, 1; Scissors, 1.
A beret, a cardboard paint palette, and a splatter-painted smock.
How to make it
Draw the palette shape on the cardboard, and check the size against the forearm before cutting. Cut the palette out.
Paint dabs of bright color around the palette edge, and flick a little paint onto the smock for splatters. Use washable paint only, and cover the table before splattering.
Wear the smock and the tilted beret, and carry the palette and brush.
Build this costume →
Fuzzy Monster
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 pastel fuzzy sweatsuit; 2 large googly eyes, 3 inches or bigger; 1 sheet white felt, 9x12 inches, for the smile; Scissors, 1 pair; Fabric glue, 1 tube, or 4 safety pins.
A pastel fuzzy sweatsuit with giant googly eyes and an oversized stitched smile.
How to make it
Glue or pin the two big googly eyes to the hood.
Draw the smile on paper first, and check the size against the chest. An adult cuts the big stitched smile from the white felt.
Glue the smile to the chest, and wear the hood up so the eyes sit above the forehead.

Questions, answered
What should a toddler costume never include? Nothing itchy, nothing that covers the face, nothing with small parts, and nothing they cannot sit in. If it fails the car-seat test, redesign it.
How do I get a toddler into costume without a meltdown? Do the fiddly bits while they nap and save dress-up for five minutes before you leave. Build the costume over normal warm clothes so there is no bare-skin battle.
Will it survive the stroller? Keep the silhouette soft and compact: no wide wings, no trailing fabric, no tall hats. Bulky extras come off in the first ten minutes, so plan the costume to look finished without them.

Updated November 2026 · Pick My Costume
Face Paint Costume Ideas
When the costume is mostly face paint, the outfit can be dead simple, black clothes plus a painted skeleton face beats a store-bought suit every time.
Use proper face paint or makeup, not craft paint or markers, and do a small patch test on the jaw an hour before in case of sensitive skin. Paint the base first, let it set, then add details, and keep makeup wipes in your pocket because touch-ups are part of the deal.
Every costume below leans on the paint job, lists the rest honestly, and links to a full build guide with real hands-on time. The brush is the costume.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Copy these costumes
Basketball Star
⏱ 5 min hands-on Easy
You need: Basketball jersey or numbered tank top, 1; Basketball shorts, 1 pair; Black non-toxic face paint or 1 eyeliner pencil; Basketball, 1.
Jersey, shorts, eye-black stripes, and a ball that never leaves your hand.
How to make it
Pull on the basketball jersey and shorts.
Draw two short black stripes under each eye with non-toxic face paint. Keep the stripes below the eye, never on the eyelid, and skip them for very young kids who will rub their eyes.
Carry the basketball tucked under one arm, and dribble it whenever you stand still.
Build this costume →
Ninja
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: All-black outfit: t-shirt, pants, and a black beanie, 1 set; Black belt or sash, 1; Black headband or strip of black t-shirt, 1 strip about 3 inches wide; Scissors, 1 pair, and tape, 1 roll; Black non-toxic face paint for a mask stripe, 1 tube.
All black with a belt sash and a slit headband.
How to make it
Dress all in black and tie the sash around the waist.
Wrap the black strip around the forehead, with eyes and mouth uncovered.
Paint a thin black stripe across the nose if you like.
Build this costume →
Boxer
⏱ 10 min hands-on Easy
You need: Bathrobe, 1; Toy boxing gloves, 1 pair; Purple and yellow non-toxic face paint, 1 tube each; Athletic shorts and sneakers, 1 set; Phone for entrance music, 1.
Bathrobe, toy gloves, bruise makeup, and entrance music.
How to make it
Pull on the athletic shorts, sneakers, and bathrobe, with the hood up.
Dab purple and yellow non-toxic face paint on one cheekbone, below one eye, never on the eyelid. One bruise only, and keep all paint clear of the eyes.
Pull on the toy boxing gloves, throw a few shadow punches, and play entrance music as you walk in.
Build this costume →
Gloom & Bloom
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 set black clothes from the closet; 1 set colorful clothes from the closet; Black and white face paint, non-toxic, 1 set; 2 hair ties for braids; 3 to 5 fake flowers.
Braids and black for Gloom, color-pop and smiles for Bloom.
How to make it
Gloom wears the black clothes and tight braids, and paints a small black teardrop under one eye. Keep the paint clear of the eyes, and test it on skin first.
Bloom wears the colorful clothes, pins the fake flowers in the hair, and paints a small flower on one cheek, clear of the eyes.
Stand side by side: Gloom frowns, Bloom smiles big.
Build this costume →
Mystery Crew
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Orange, purple, blue, and red t-shirts, 1 each; Dog ears headband or a brown dog costume piece, 1; Fake magnifying glass, 1; Headband or scarf in a matching color, 1 per person; Brown non-toxic face paint for the dog's nose, 1 tube.
Assign the leader, the style icon, the brains, the goofball, and one very good dog.
How to make it
Assign the roles: orange for the leader, purple for the style icon, blue for the brains, red for the goofball. The dog wears the ears headband.
Each person puts on their color t-shirt and a matching headband or scarf, tied loose, never tight. The brains carries the fake magnifying glass.
Paint a brown nose on the dog with non-toxic face paint, keeping it clear of the eyes. Line up with the dog in front, and point at something suspicious.
Build this costume →
Deadpan Diva
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Black dress, 1; Very pale foundation or white non-toxic face paint, 1; Dark eyeliner and lipstick, 1 set; 2 hair ties; Thin black ribbon, 1 short length (optional, for the choker; buy: craft store).
Black dress, two braids, pale makeup, and a stare that ends conversations.
How to make it
Braid the hair into two tight braids. Test the pale foundation on the jawline first, then put it on evenly and blend it into the neck.
Add the dark eyeliner and lipstick, and put on the black dress. Use skin-safe makeup only, and wash it all off before bed.
Fold the arms and hold the stare. Add reflective tape or a glow stick, and carry a flashlight for visibility at night.
Build this costume →

⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: 2 headbands; 1 sheet black craft felt, 9x12 inches; 1 sheet gray craft felt, 9x12 inches; Black eyeliner pencil or non-toxic face paint, 1; Scissors, 1 pair; Tape, 1 roll; Pink felt, 1 small triangle (optional, for inner ears; buy: craft store).
Cat ears versus mouse ears. Spend the night chasing each other.

Tape one pair of ears to each headband, and put the headbands on.

Plumber Duo
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Blue overalls, 2; Red t-shirt and green t-shirt, 1 each; Red cap and green cap, 1 each; Brown non-toxic face paint for mustaches, 1 tube; White circle stickers or white paper, 2 about 2 inches across; Marker, 1.
Overalls, red and green caps and shirts, drawn mustaches.
How to make it
Write a big M on one white circle and an L on the other, and stick or tape them to the red cap and the green cap.
Each brother wears blue overalls over their colored t-shirt and cap.
Paint on the mustaches with brown non-toxic face paint: a big bushy one for red, a thinner one for green. Keep the paint clear of the eyes, and test it on skin first.
Build this costume →
Little Witch
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: Black cape or black bedsheet, 1; Pointy witch hat, 1; Black-and-white striped tights, 1 pair; Green non-toxic face paint, 1 tube; Safety pin or ribbon, 1.
Black cape, pointy hat, striped tights, green face paint.
How to make it
Pin or tie the black cape at the shoulders, loose at the neck.
Paint the nose, chin, and forehead lightly green. Use non-toxic face paint only, and keep it clear of the eyes.
Pull on the striped tights and the pointy hat.
Build this costume →
Good Witch, Bad Witch
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: 1 black dress or set of black clothes for the bad witch; 1 pink dress or set of pink clothes for the good witch; Green face paint, non-toxic, 1 tube; 1 cardboard crown; 1 black cone hat; Hot glue gun, scissors, 1 pink marker, tape.
Green face paint and black for one, pink gown and crown for the other.
How to make it
Bad witch: wear black, and paint the face and hands green with non-toxic paint. Keep the paint away from the eyes, and patch test sensitive skin first.
An adult folds the black hat brim and hot glues it in place. Hot glue sets in seconds, so check the fit in a mirror first.
Good witch: wear pink, color the cardboard crown with the pink marker, and tape it on.
Build this costume →

Remind me
Questions, answered
Can I use craft paint or markers on skin? No. Use proper face paint or makeup, and do a small patch test on the jaw an hour before in case of sensitive skin. Craft paint can irritate and stain.
What order do I paint in? Base first, let it set, then details. Details painted onto wet base bleed; details painted onto set base stay crisp.
How do I keep it from smearing all night? Keep makeup wipes in your pocket because touch-ups are part of the deal, and set the finished paint with a light dusting of translucent powder.
Own the supplies already? Check the Pantry to see which of all 169 costumes you can make tonight from what is in your house. Or wander the costume galaxy .

Pick My Costume

Easy DIY Halloween Costumes, Filtered by What You Already Own
Updated September 2026
Don't start from the store. Start from the junk drawer. Tick the materials you already have and all 169 costume ideas re-rank around what you own: fully covered builds first, then the ones missing just a supply or two.
Every materials list below is the real one from that costume's build guide, and the build times are the real ones too. No guessing, no "easy" hand-waving.
We assume you have the 12 household basics: scissors, tape (any kind), paper and pen, markers, aluminum foil, cardboard / boxes, white t-shirt, t-shirt (any color), black clothes, old bedsheet, pillowcase, socks. Untick anything you don't actually own on the pantry page , which fine-tunes every costume.

Tap everything you already own. Builds you can make right now jump to the top.

2. In a hurry tonight?
If the clock matters more than the craft drawer, start with the costumes built for tonight.
Make-it-tonight builds
126 of the 169 ideas are make-tonight : 30 minutes or less of hands-on work, two hours or less total. The Classic Ghost and the Emoji Crew need zero extra shopping.
See the make-it-tonight costumes
Or tick everything you own on the pantry page →
FAQ
How does the materials filter work?
Tick the supplies you already own and every one of the 169 costumes is re-ranked by what it still needs: fully covered builds lead, then builds missing one or two supplies, then the rest. The materials lists are the real ones from each costume's build guide.
What household basics do you assume I have?
Scissors, tape, markers, paper and pen, aluminum foil, cardboard, a white t-shirt, a plain t-shirt, black clothes, an old bedsheet, a pillowcase, and socks. These 12 staples are assumed present on this page; the pantry page lets you untick anything you don't actually have.
Do any costumes need zero extra shopping?
Yes. Two builds are make-tonight from the household basics alone: the Classic Ghost (a white sheet with cut-out eyes) and the Emoji Crew (a yellow tee, a paper plate, and markers). Fifteen more need just 1 or 2 supplies, so one quick store run covers all 17.
Can I also filter by build time?
Yes. The build-time chips use the real build times from each costume's guide: show only costumes that take 30 minutes or less, or an hour or less.
Where do the materials lists come from?
Every costume on Pick My Costume has a full DIY build guide with a materials list and numbered steps. This page reuses those same lists, so what you see here matches the guide you'll open.
Not sure where to start?
The 2-minute quiz picks 3 costume ideas from the bank of 169, free, no signup.

Questions, answered
What makes a costume read as funny? Commitment. A name tag, a prop, or one bad pun delivered deadpan sells it. Half-measures read as confused, not funny.
Can a funny costume still be easy? Yes. Most of the picks below take 30 minutes or less of hands-on work. Funny comes from the idea, not the effort.
What if our group cannot agree on one funny idea? Pick a theme with roles, like Ketchup and Mustard or the Office Couple. Everyone gets their own part and the photo still reads as one joke.
Not sure which one? Take the 2-minute quiz and get your match. Or wander the costume galaxy .

Questions, answered
What counts as easy here? Builds rated Easy in our bank, most under 30 minutes of hands-on work. Times are estimates from the guide; yours may vary.

Remind me
Questions, answered
What makes these costumes glow? Glow-in-the-dark tape and bracelets, glow-in-the-dark temporary tattoos, and battery tea lights. Each guide lists exactly what to get.
Are they safe for trick-or-treating? They are more visible than most costumes, which drivers appreciate. Keep face openings wide and props soft.
How long does the glow last? Glow tape charges in light and fades over a few hours. Hold it under a lamp for 10 minutes before heading out for a recharge. The battery tea lights in two of the builds stay lit without charging.
Not sure which one? Take the 2-minute quiz and get your match. Or wander the costume galaxy .

Questions, answered
What makes a costume read as cute? Soft shapes, round features, and one oversized detail. Animal ears, a tutu, or a plush texture do the work; the build underneath can stay simple.
Are these only for kids? Most of the picks below are kid and family favorites, but cute scales up. A ladybug or a chipmunk works at any age with the right sizing.
Can I make one tonight? Yes, most of these take 30 minutes or less of hands-on work. Check the time chip on each card; anything that has to dry needs a head start.
Not sure which one? Take the 2-minute quiz and get your match. Or wander the costume galaxy .

Questions, answered
I want cute, not scary. What should I pick? Start with the Black Cat Burglar or the Tooth Fairy. Both read instantly and neither needs horror makeup.
What works for a duo or group? Good Witch Bad Witch and the Witchy Sisters give everyone a distinct role with one shared theme. The Tooth Fairy plus Tooth is a classic couple pick.
How much time do these take? Hands-on time runs 15 to 45 minutes. Check the time chip on each card; anything that has to dry needs a head start.

How much time do these take? Hands-on time runs 10 to 30 minutes. Check the time chip on each card; anything that has to dry needs a head start.

What makes a costume read as goth? Black clothing, pale makeup, and a calm stare. The look is mostly attitude: one dark outfit worn like you mean it does more than a pile of accessories.
Is there a goth costume for a kid? Yes. The Goth Schoolgirl pairs a plaid skirt and black cardigan with braided pigtails and pale makeup. For a duo, Gloom & Bloom puts one wearer in braids and black while the other goes bright.

How to Make a Witch Costume
Short answer: a pointy hat, a dark base you already own, and one strong color. The hat does most of the work; everything else is range.
A kid witch takes 15 minutes with a black cape and a bought hat. The adult green witch goes bigger: a long green dress, a hat shaped from black cardboard, dramatic makeup, 45 minutes. Two of you can split into a good witch and a bad witch in 20 minutes, one in pink, one in black with green face paint. Three of you can run the full sister trio in 35.
Every build below lists the real hands-on time and exactly what you need, and links to the full step-by-step guide.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Little Witch
⏱ 15 min hands-on Easy
You need: 5 things in all.
Black cape, pointy hat, striped tights, green face paint.
Build this costume →
Emerald Witch
⏱ 45 min hands-on Medium
You need: 6 things in all.
An all-green-everything gown, dramatic makeup, and a pointy hat gone couture. Wicked Elphaba inspired.
Build this costume →
Good Witch, Bad Witch
⏱ 20 min hands-on Easy
You need: 6 things in all.
Green face paint and black for one, pink gown and crown for the other.
Build this costume →
Witchy Sister Trio
⏱ 35 min hands-on Easy
You need: 5 things in all.
Three color-coded witch dresses: green, purple, and orange.
Build this costume →
Which witch fits you?
One wearer under ten: start with the Little Witch . It is the fastest build here and the cape can be cut from a black bedsheet. One adult going all in: the Emerald Witch , the green one everyone photographs. Two or three of you: the Good Witch, Bad Witch duo splits pink against black, and the Witchy Sister Trio gives each sister her own color.
🔔 One email on Oct 27
Want one email on Oct 27 with costumes you can make that night? That’s it, one email, then you’re off the list.
Remind me
Questions, answered
How long does it take to make a witch costume? The fastest build here is the Little Witch at 15 minutes of hands-on time. The duo takes 20 minutes, the trio 35, and the Emerald Witch 45. Every card shows the real hands-on time from its guide.
Do I need to buy a pointy hat? Not always. The Little Witch and the sister trio use a bought hat, but the Emerald Witch guide shapes the hat from a sheet of black cardboard. A hat left over from an old costume works for any of them.
What makes an outfit read as a witch costume? The pointy hat. A black dress or cape alone reads as formal; add the hat and it reads witch from across the street. Green face paint is the second signal: it turns the same outfit into the wicked version.
Can kids wear these witch costumes? The Little Witch is built for kids, with a cape cut from a black bedsheet or t-shirt and a bought hat. The duo and trio scale down too, and every guide lists its own safety notes.

What Can I Be for Halloween With a Black Dress?
Short answer: a black dress plus one strong signal. The dress alone reads as a dress. Add two braids and pale makeup and it reads deadpan diva in 15 minutes. Add black tights and braids and it is the goth braids look in 20. A long black gown pairs up into a goth couple in 30, and the same closet turns wicked as the bad witch in a good witch, bad witch duo in 20. Every build below starts from a black dress you already own, lists the real hands-on time and what else you need, and links to the full step-by-step guide.

Questions, answered
What is the fastest black dress costume here? The Deadpan Diva at 15 minutes of hands-on time: black dress, two braids, pale makeup, done. The goth braids look takes 20, the duo 20, and the goth couple 30.
Will a black dress on its own read as a costume? No. On its own it reads as a dress. Each build here adds one loud signal on top: braids and pale makeup, a streaked wig and neck bolts, or green face paint. The signal is the costume.
Do I need a special kind of black dress? No. The diva and braids builds use a plain black dress you own. The goth couple uses a long black dress or gown, and thrifted is fine. The bad witch half of the duo works with any black dress or set of black clothes.
Are any of these black dress costumes for two people? Two of them. The Macabre Goth Couple is built for two, and Good Witch, Bad Witch pairs your black dress with a partner in pink.

Already at home

Questions, answered
Which hoodie color covers the most costumes? Green. The Baby Dinosaur, the Raptor Barista, and the dinosaur half of Dino Rangers all start from a green hoodie. Gray covers two, the Little Shark and Crowd Camouflage, and black covers two more, the Neon Demon Hunter and Error 404.
Do I have to sew anything? No. Nothing on this page needs a needle. The spikes, fins, and ears go on with tape, safety pins, or fabric glue, and the Web Hero Crew is paint and stickers on sunglasses. Pinned pieces come off the same night, so the hoodie goes back in the drawer.
What is the fastest costume on this page? Crowd Camouflage takes five minutes: gray hoodie, dark pants, a beanie, and a name tag you leave blank. Error 404 and the Raptor Barista take ten minutes each. The rest run fifteen to thirty minutes of hands-on time.
Which of these are made for kids? Four. The Baby Dinosaur, the Little Shark, and the Blue Heeler Pup are written for kids, and the kids in Dino Rangers wear the green hoodies while the grown-ups wear khaki. The Blue Heeler guide uses face paint, never a mask, so small kids can see and breathe.

Warm Halloween Costume Ideas
Halloween night is cold in most of the country, and a costume that only works over a t-shirt fails by the second block.
Every costume below is built to layer: cloaks over coats, fuzzy suits over sweats, hoods and hats that hold real warmth. Each one lists exactly what you need and links to a full build guide with real hands-on time.
Pick for the forecast, not just the photo.

Remind me
Questions, answered
How do you keep a costume warm without ruining it? Build the costume one size loose and put the warm layer under it, not over it. A coat under a cloak still reads as a cloak; a coat over a costume hides it. Thermals under a sweatsuit disappear completely.
What is the warmest costume on this page? The Fuzzy Monster and the Penguin Huddle. Both are full sweatsuits with hoods, so they take a thermal layer and gloves with nothing showing. The Astronaut covers head to toe as well.
Can these work for toddlers? Yes. The Little Lion and the Penguin Huddle are built for small kids, with hoods instead of masks and room for a warm layer under the costume on the coldest nights.
Do I need to sew anything? No. These builds use tape, glue, and safety pins. Where a seam would help, the guide offers a pin or tape fix that lasts the night.

Each build lists what you need and links to a full guide with real hands-on time. No size charts, no squeezing.

Remind me
Questions, answered
How do I make sure a DIY costume fits? Measure the wearer, not a size chart. The guides size each piece to the person: sheet length from shoulder to ankle, board width across the shoulders. Cut big and trim; you cannot add fabric back.
Which costumes are the most forgiving? The Classic Ghost, the Classic Wizard, and the Garden Gnome. All three drape from the shoulders with a belt or sash to set the shape, so they fit the same way at any size.
Are the food costumes comfortable to sit in? The Donut and the Pizza Slice hang from shoulder straps and leave your back free, so sitting and driving work. The Coffee Cup is a tube; pick it for standing parties, not long car rides.
Do I need special plus-size supplies? No. You may need a bigger sheet or board for the same build, and the guides say where. Everything else is the standard craft list.

Remind me
Questions, answered
Why do schools ban masks? Teachers need to see faces, and masks block side vision on stairs and in crowds. These costumes keep the face fully open, so they pass most school rules. Check your school letter to be sure.
Do any of these need face paint? No. Face paint is optional on a few and required on none. The Ballerina, the Cheerleader, and the Referee read from the outfit and the props alone.
Will these work with glasses? Yes. Nothing sits on the face, so glasses stay on all night. The Pirate Captain and the Referee read fine with the wearer's own glasses.
Are these good for toddlers? The Tiny Firefighter, the Little Baker, and the Ballerina are built for toddlers: hats come off fast, nothing covers the mouth or nose, and bathroom breaks stay simple.

Remind me
Questions, answered
How do you size one theme for different ages? Build each kid's piece in their own size from the same colors and materials. The guides size per wearer, so a seven-year-old's dino and a three-year-old's dino match without either one swimming in it.
What works for three or more siblings? The Chipmunk Trio, the Dino Herd, and the Ice Kingdom Crew are written for groups. Each kid gets a color or a role, and extra kids slot in without changing the theme.
What if one sibling wants scary and one wants cute? Try the Witchy Sister Trio: it is built on contrast, one dark and one bright. Cat & Mouse also pairs a chaser and a runner, so different moods still match.
Can twins wear the exact same costume? Yes. Salt & Pepper and Ketchup & Mustard are true pairs with mirrored builds. Make both at once from one supply run, and the two builds take less time than two separate costumes.

Sweatsuit Costume Ideas
One sweatsuit in one solid color is the most useful costume base in the house. It is warm, it stays comfortable all night, and it comes in the wearer’s real size. Add felt, tape, and one or two props and the same base turns into a monster, a lion, an astronaut, or a banana. Every costume below starts from a single sweatsuit, lists exactly what else you need, and links to a full build guide with real hands-on time. Pick the color first: black alone covers the skeleton, the spider, and the bee.

Remind me
Questions, answered
Which sweatsuit color covers the most costumes? Black. The Glow Skeleton, the Eight-Legged Spider, and the Bumble Bee all start from a black sweatsuit or a black sweatshirt and sweatpants. White makes the Astronaut, yellow makes the Banana, and any solid color makes the Spaceship Cadet.
Do I have to sew anything? No. Every build on this page works with fabric glue, tape, or safety pins. Where a guide lists a needle, glue is named as the alternative, and several guides offer safety pins as the first choice.
Can I wear the sweatsuit again after Halloween? Yes, if you pin instead of glue. Pinned and taped pieces come off the same night. The Spider is the keeper: its eight sock legs glue or stitch to the sweatshirt, so that sweatsuit stays a costume.
Are sweatsuit costumes warm enough for trick-or-treating? Yes. A sweatsuit is already a full layer, and there is room for thermals under it without changing the look. It is the warmest cheap base on the site, which is why so many of these builds are made for kids.

Questions, answered
Which dress colors cover the most costumes? Black and white cover the most ground. A black dress starts the Deadpan Diva and the gown half of the Macabre Goth Couple. A white dress starts the Ice Skater and the fairy half of the Tooth Fairy. Green starts both the Emerald Witch and one of the three Witchy Sisters.
Do I have to sew anything? No. One build even mentions sewing: the Emerald Witch, where hot glue does the same job on the gown and the hat. The other nine builds are wear, paint, tape, and pin. The Fairy Tale crowns are cut from a cereal box and taped shut.
Can one of these cost nothing? Yes. The Deadpan Diva can cost nothing: a black dress from your own closet, two braids, and pale makeup only if it is already in your drawer. The Fairy Tale Princesses run close behind: any closet dress plus a crown cut from a cereal box.
How many of these are group costumes? Seven of the ten are built for two or more people: a princess per dress, an ice kingdom with four roles, three color-coded witch sisters, a goth couple, a mermaid crew, a tooth and her fairy, and a head-to-toe pink crew. The Emerald Witch, the Deadpan Diva, and the Ice Skater are solo builds.

Which t-shirt color covers the most costumes? Yellow. One yellow t-shirt per person builds the whole Emoji Crew and the whole Yellow Henchmen Crew, and a yellow tee is the mustard half of Ketchup and Mustard. White starts the Deviled Egg, and green fills a whole pod of peas.

Baby Pumpkin Costume
Start with the costume parents actually came for last Halloween: Baby Pumpkin was the site’s most-viewed costume of the 2026 season. The build is below, not behind a quiz: an orange onesie, green felt leaves, a brown felt stem, and light stuffing, pinned where you can see every pin. It takes 20 minutes of hands-on time. If pumpkin is not your baby, eight more first-Halloween builds follow, each with its own photo, time, supplies, and full guide.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Start here: Baby Pumpkin, the full build
This is the whole build. Keep the stuffing between layers, never against the skin, and check the pins and the baby’s neck as the guide says.
⏱ 20 min Easy
An orange onesie, green felt leaves, and the easiest first Halloween ever.
What you need
Orange onesie or footed pajamas, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
Green craft felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
Soft stuffing or an old pillow, 1 (own)
Brown felt for the stem, 1 small piece (buy: craft store)
Safety pins, 4 (buy: dollar store)
Scissors, 1 pair
Build it, step by step
Lightly stuff the arms and legs, between layers. Never put stuffing against the skin.
Cut leaf shapes from the green felt.
Pin the leaves around the collar.
Roll the brown felt into a stem.
Pin the stem to the top of the hood or a soft hat.
Safety: Keep all pins on the outside of the onesie where you can see them, and never pin near the baby's skin. Skip small parts a baby could pull off. Check every pin stays closed before and during wear. Feel the baby's neck often. Take the stuffing out if they feel hot.
Optional pro finish: photograph the pumpkin in a laundry basket lined with a blanket.

Questions, answered
Is the stuffing safe for a baby? Use it the way the guide says: lightly stuff the arms and legs between layers, never against the skin. Keep every safety pin on the outside where you can see it, skip small parts a baby could pull off, and take the stuffing out if the baby feels hot.
Do I need to sew the Baby Pumpkin? No. The leaves and stem pin on with four safety pins. Pin from the outside, check that every pin stays closed, and keep the pins away from the baby's skin.
Does the Baby Pumpkin need face paint? No. The lead build uses no face paint. Little Lion paints a nose and whiskers and says to skip paint for under-twos and any child who rubs their face; Little Pig Family uses a little blush or face paint on cheeks.
How long do the other builds take? The eight alternatives run 20 to 40 minutes of hands-on time. Little Lion, Bumble Bee, Pocket Plush Monster, and Fuzzy Gremlin Plush also name drying time for glue.

Coffee Cup Costume
The whole coffee cup build is on this page: a white sheet or large white bag, a cardboard tube, and a brown paper lid, in 20 minutes. It reads at ten feet, and it pairs naturally with a donut. Below it are nine more breakfast builds for one person, a pair, or a group, each with its own photo, hands-on time, supply list, and guide.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Start here: Coffee Cup, the full build
For a child under eight, follow the guide’s safety swap and use a white sheet, not a trash bag.
⏱ 20 min Easy
White trash bag over a cardboard tube, brown lid hat.
What you need
White trash bag or white sheet, 1 large (make: from home)
Cardboard tube or large cylinder, 1 (make: from home)
Brown paper or felt for the lid, 1 sheet (buy: craft store)
Brown marker, 1 thick (buy: dollar store)
Build it, step by step
Cut the arm holes first.
Then cut the head hole small.
Hold the bag up to test the size. Never pull it over the head.
Cut the holes in the white trash bag for head and arms.
Safety: Cut the head hole wide enough. The wearer must see and breathe with ease. Wear the bag over clothes, never on bare skin. Use a white sheet for kids under 8. Take it off if you feel hot.
This is the cup.
A head hole cut too big slides off the shoulders.
Draw a coffee shop logo on the front with brown marker.
Make the lid: cut a brown paper circle bigger than your head, with a sip hole.
Wear the bag.
Put the lid hat on top.
Optional pro finish: cut a cardboard sleeve, write a coffee-shop pun on it, and tape it around the torso.

Remind me
Questions, answered
What should a child use instead of a trash bag? A white sheet. The Coffee Cup guide says to use a white sheet for kids under 8, wear it over clothes, cut the head hole wide enough for easy seeing and breathing, and take it off if the wearer feels hot.
Do any of these need sewing? No build needs stitching. They use cutting, tape, safety pins, glue, and paint. The Milk & Cookies list mentions a sewing kit only as a place to find its four safety pins.
Can I make the coffee cup as a pair? Yes. Donut & Coffee is the built pair on this page: one person wears the pink frosted ring and the other wears the takeout cup. Bacon & Eggs, Peanut Butter & Jelly, and Milk & Cookies are also two-person builds.
How long does the lead build take? 20 minutes of hands-on time and no drying time. Six of the alternatives name drying time for paint or glue, from 20 minutes to an hour.

Pickle Costume
The pickle is a green tunic plus texture: about twenty bumps glued in a loose grid, green face paint, and a smug grin. The full build is below, with the hands-on and drying time named up front. If a whole produce aisle sounds better, nine more food builds follow, including a peas-in-a-pod group costume for three to five people.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Start here: Pickle, the full build
Lay the bumps out dry first. The guide’s loose grid is what stops bare patches from showing.
⏱ 30 min + 1 hr drying Easy
Green tunic, bumpy texture, smug grin.
What you need
Green tunic or oversized green t-shirt, 1 (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
Green bubble wrap or green pom-poms, about 20 bumps (buy: craft store, or make: twist bits of green fabric)
Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
Green non-toxic face paint, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)
Build it, step by step
Lay all the bumps on the tunic dry first.
Step back and check.
Glue the bumps all over the front and back of the tunic.
Space them in a loose grid so no bare patches show.
Let the fabric glue dry flat for 30 minutes.
Paint the face.
Safety: Keep the green paint clear of eyes. Wash the paint off that night.
Draw on a smug grin with one raised eyebrow.
Wear the tunic over regular clothes.
Stand tall.
Optional pro finish: add a darker green felt band at the top and bottom of the tunic.

Questions, answered
What can I use for the bumps? Green bubble wrap or green pom-poms, about twenty bumps. If you have neither, the guide lets you twist bits of green fabric instead.
When can I wear it? Plan on 30 minutes of hands-on time plus drying time for the fabric glue. Let the tunic dry flat before wearing it.
Can I make it a group costume? Yes. Peas in a Pod is written for three to five people, Fruit Salad Crew gives every person a fruit color and a leaf hat, and Chips & Guac is a two-person build.
Do I need to sew? No. The Pickle glues on. Across this page, the fasteners are fabric glue, hot glue in the two builds that name it, tape, and safety pins.

Cardboard Knight Costume
The knight starts with the boxes people already have: two or three large ones become a chest plate, back plate, shoulders, and helmet. Silver paint and black marker lines do the metal work, and the sword is a pool noodle wrapped in gray tape. The full build is below. Nine more cardboard costumes follow if your box pile points somewhere else.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Start here: Cardboard Knight, the full build
An adult handles the heavy cutting. The guide is blunt about the helmet: cut the eye holes wide, because cardboard cannot be added back.
⏱ 60 min + 1 hr drying Medium
Silver-painted cardboard armor and a pool-noodle sword.
What you need
Large cardboard boxes, 2 to 3 (make: collect spares)
Silver acrylic paint, 1 bottle (buy: craft store, tempera paint works too)
Foam brush or paintbrush, 1 wide (own, or buy: craft store)
1 pool noodle (buy: toy store or dollar store)
Gray duct tape, 1 roll (buy: dollar store)
Black marker, 1 (buy: dollar store)
Scissors, 1 pair
Build it, step by step
Safety: An adult should handle the heavy cutting. Cut generous eye holes in the helmet so vision stays clear.
Draw every piece on the cardboard before cutting: chest plate, back plate, shoulders, helmet.
Cut the helmet eye holes wide. Cardboard cannot be added back.
A knight who cannot see is a hazard.
Cut all the pieces.
Paint every armor piece silver.
Let the paint dry fully.
Add rivet dots and edge lines with the black marker.
Tape the plates together so they hinge at the shoulders.
Wrap the pool noodle in gray duct tape for the sword.
Safety: Swing the noodle sword in open space only. Never swing it at faces.
Put the armor on over dark clothes.
Carry the noodle sword.
Optional pro finish: tape a red crepe-paper plume to the helmet top.

Questions, answered
How many boxes do I need? Two to three large cardboard boxes for the knight: chest plate, back plate, shoulders, and helmet. Paint every piece silver and add rivet dots and edge lines with the black marker.
Is the sword safe around other kids? It is a pool noodle wrapped in gray duct tape. The guide's rule is open space only and never swing it at faces.
Who should cut the armor? An adult should handle the heavy cutting. Cut generous eye holes in the helmet so vision stays clear, and test the helmet before the paint goes on.
How long does it take? 60 minutes of hands-on time plus an hour for paint to dry fully. Block Monster and Tiny Snail are faster alternatives at 30 minutes of hands-on time.

Haunted Animatronics Costume
Each animatronic is a big cardboard box painted gray with black scuffs and cracks, a wide jagged mouth, and two red LED tea lights glowing through the eye holes. Old torn clothes and short jerky moves finish it. The complete build is below, including the safety rules that matter with a box over your head. Nine more haunted and robot builds follow.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Start here: Haunted Animatronics, the full build
Adults handle the utility knife and the hot glue. That is this page’s hard rule, not a footnote.
⏱ 60 min + 1 hr drying Medium
Glitchy mascot heads from cardboard boxes, flickering LED eyes, jerky moves.
What you need
1 large cardboard box per person, big enough to cover the head (make: use what you own)
2 red LED tea lights per person (buy: dollar store)
Paint in gray, black, and one accent color, 1 small bottle each (buy: craft store)
1 set old clothes with holes or tears (make: use what you own)
Hot glue gun, 1; scissors, 1 pair; utility knife, 1 (adults only)
Build it, step by step
Safety: An adult handles the utility knife and the hot glue for every cut and glue step.
Mark the eye holes and the wide jagged mouth on the outside of the box first.
Have the wearer hold the box up.
Check the eye spots before cutting.
Cut the eye holes wide and the mouth wide, adults only. Cardboard cannot be put back.
Small eye holes make a blind hazard.
Paint the box gray with black scuffs and cracks.
Glue one red LED tea light inside each eye hole.
Safety: Make the eye holes large, and never wear the box near stairs or traffic, since side vision is limited. Walk with a partner who can see clearly. Take the box off if you feel hot.
Wear the box over the head, eyes lined up with the holes.
Wear the old clothes with holes underneath.
Move in short jerky steps.
Freeze between moves.
Optional pro finish: paint black scuffs and cracks around the eye holes before adding the lights.

Questions, answered
How does each person see? Cut the eye holes large and line them up before wearing. Side vision is limited, so the guide says to walk with a partner who can see clearly and never wear the box near stairs or traffic.
Who handles the cutting and glue? An adult handles the utility knife and hot glue for every cut and glue step. Mark the eye holes and mouth before cutting, and check the eye spots with the wearer holding the box up.
How many tea lights does each costume need? Two red LED tea lights per person, one glued inside each eye hole.
What if I do not want a box on my head? Haunted Portraits uses old-fashioned dark clothes, gray face paint, and a frame. Glow Skeleton uses a black sweatsuit and glow tape. Both are on this page.

Updated November 2026 · Pick My Costume
Pizza Slice Costume
The slice is a cardboard triangle about three feet tall: golden paint, red felt pepperoni, a brown crust strip at the wide end, and string loops so it wears like a sandwich board. The complete build is below. Nine more food builds follow, most of them made for two people to wear together.
Can't pick? Take the 2-minute quiz → Free. No signup.
Start here: Pizza Slice, the full build
Keep the crust at the top and the point at the bottom. That one orientation choice is what makes the triangle read as pizza.
⏱ 45 min + 1 hr drying Medium
A big cardboard triangle, painted golden with felt pepperoni.
What you need
Large cardboard box, 1 (make: cut a big triangle, about 3 feet tall)
Yellow and orange acrylic paint, 1 bottle each (buy: craft store)
Red felt, 1 sheet (buy: craft store; red paper works too)
Brown felt scraps for crust, or 1 brown paper bag (buy: craft store)
Paintbrush, scissors, tape, 1 set (own)
Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
Build it, step by step
Paint the whole triangle a golden yellow-orange.
Let it dry 1 hour.
Arrange the pepperoni on the triangle dry first.
Cut red felt circles.
Safety: Let an adult cut the felt circles. Keep fingers clear of the scissors.
Glue them spread out.
Add the brown crust strip along the wide end.
Tape two string loops to the back so it wears like a sandwich board.
Keep the crust at the top and the point at the bottom.
Optional pro finish: add green felt peppers and white felt cheese drips along the top edge.

Questions, answered
Which end is up? The crust goes at the top and the point at the bottom. Tape two string loops to the back so the triangle wears like a sandwich board.
How big should the slice be? About three feet tall, cut from one large cardboard box. Paint it golden yellow-orange and let the paint dry for an hour before the pepperoni and crust go on.
Can two people match? Yes. Burger & Fries, Donut & Coffee, Chips & Guac, Sushi & Soy Sauce, Milk & Cookies, S'mores Duo, and Wine & Cheese are all built for two or more people.
Do I need to sew? No build on this page needs stitching. They use glue, tape, paint, safety pins, and straps.
